families.description: Find samples by type, attribute, treatment, keyword, lab code or UID. No assay: assay lives on DERIVED_FROM and belongs to graph_traversal.

groups.name: Find samples by attribute, keyword or lab

capabilities.name: Attribute / keyword sample search (mode=new_search)
capabilities.description: Search and filter samples by sample type code, assay, treatment, free-text keyword, lab/PI code or UID against POST /nextseek_api/samples/advanced_search/. Returns paginated rows with json_metadata. The broad catch-all retrieval route; explicitly read-only.
enum_values: filter_matchType: PARTIAL (default; mandated for text/keyword/lab searches)
endpoint timeout raised 90s -> 120s for advanced_search only
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re \b195\b
capabilities.example_query: Find me mice treated with NDMA.

capabilities.name: NExtSEEK REST request tool (the read door) and its allow/block list
capabilities.description: The single function the whole nextseek_query engine uses to talk to NExtSEEK/SEEK: validates the body against the cached OpenAPI schema, sends with basic auth, unwraps legacy <a href> HTML out of UID-bearing fields (uid, uuid, title, idlink, idurl), and returns {ok, url, status_code, method, query, body, data}. All GETs are allowed; only three POST paths are read-allowlisted.
enum_values: sanitized HTML fields: uid, uuid, title, idlink, idurl
error shape: {ok:false, error_type:'schema_validation', provided_fields, unknown_fields, missing_required_fields, allowed_fields}
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_result_meta.status_code eq 200
capabilities.example_query: Show me the metadata for sample D.SEQ-240910LAU-1.
capabilities.gap: The allow/block list cannot be observed from a chat turn: a blocked path is never attempted, so nothing distinguishes 'refused by the door' from 'never chosen by the parser'. The door's own refusal envelope {ok:false, error_type:'schema_validation', unknown_fields, missing_required_fields, allowed_fields} is built in chat_nextseek/helpers/tools/nextseek_api.py:tool_nextseek_api_request and then discarded — helpers/results.py:build_api_result_meta keeps only ok/status_code/url/row_count/bundle_id/total_matching/truncated. Needs api_result_meta.error_type.

capabilities.name: Compile a routed plan into a schema-valid HTTP request (and repair it)
capabilities.description: The api_agent turns the chosen endpoint plus parser filters into method/requestBody/queryParameters, schema-first from the endpoint's registered schema and the enriched catalog entry. Four deterministic post-LLM repairs: decline rather than fire an empty body at a body-requiring endpoint; collapse a list-valued filter_searchText; back-fill advanced_search's filter_searchText from parser keywords (an empty string matched all 50,886 samples); fall back to the schema default method on a disallowed one.
enum_values: APIRequestPlan fields: endpoint, method, requestBody, queryParameters, notes
decline sentinel: endpoint=None with 'Structured parsing failed and {endpoint} requires a request body; no request was attempted'
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_plan.requestBody.filter_searchText nonempty
capabilities.example_query: Find me all CD8 antibodies in the database.
capabilities.gap: Asserts the exact measured repair: an empty filter_searchText matched all 50,886 samples, so a blank value here IS the bug.

capabilities.name: Empty-result retry ladder (OR then SINGLE, with a ceiling)
capabilities.description: When advanced_search returns zero rows or times out, re-sends with progressively looser text: all terms OR-joined, then each term alone. Terms come from the text actually sent plus filters.keywords plus filters.lab_codes. A SINGLE-term retry returning more than 200 rows is rejected as not an answer, and any substitution is recorded so the reply can disclose that the rows are not the user's terms.
enum_values: retry label: OR (all terms joined with ' OR ')
retry label: SINGLE (one term at a time)
useless retry tokens dropped: bare digits
useless retry tokens dropped: PUB / PUB<digits>
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re (?i)(no (exact )?(results|matches|samples) (for|matching)|instead (searched|looked)|broadened|each term separately)
capabilities.example_query: Find NHP samples treated with pembrolizumab in the Shoulders study.
capabilities.gap: The ladder's own record is unreachable. _retry_advanced_search_if_empty writes retry_api_plan['retry_substituted_search'] at helpers/tools/nextseek_api.py:524, but orchestrator.py:1187 re-validates through APIRequestPlan (model_config extra='ignore') before debug_payload['api_plan'] is written, which strips the key — the code comment at orchestrator.py:1198 says so explicitly. helpers/results.py:123 turns it into disclosure['search_text_substituted'] for the chatter, and api_result_meta_truncation deliberately drops that too. So only the chatter's prose survives, which is why this criterion is a phrase-match. Needs api_result_meta.search_text_substituted.

capabilities.name: Admin-retrieve to advanced_search auto-correction
capabilities.description: A plan that chose the UID-requiring admin retrieve endpoint but produced no UIDs is rewritten to advanced_search and annotated in notes, before execution, so the turn cannot fire a guaranteed-invalid admin call.
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_plan.endpoint contains advanced_search
capabilities.example_query: Give me the full records for every RNA sample in the database.
capabilities.gap: Asserts the OUTCOME (a UID-less turn never fires the UID-requiring admin endpoint) rather than the guard's marker. parser_plan.notes contains 'endpoint auto-corrected to /samples/advanced_search/' is also observable and exactly diagnostic, but only fires when the LLM has already made the mistake, so it cannot be provoked deterministically.

capabilities.name: Lab / PI-scoped search via the 3-letter UID code
capabilities.description: A lab or PI is deliberately NOT a graph node: it is encoded as a 3-letter code inside the sample UID (Kamm -> KAM, D.SEQ-221031SHA-67 -> SHA), so lab scoping is a PARTIAL free-text filter on the UID, never a traversal and never an EXACT match. Names with fewer than 3 alphabetic characters return '' (too ambiguous).
enum_values: EntityAgentOutput.lab_codes (3-letter UID codes, filled deterministically downstream)
rule: holds even for 'how many ... in the X lab' counts
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_plan.requestBody.filter_searchText contains KAM
capabilities.example_query: How many samples are from the Kamm lab?

capabilities.name: Numeric / date comparison applied as a local post-filter
capabilities.description: REST cannot enforce >, <, between, before/after on a metadata field, so the parser anchors on the field name as a keyword and preserves the comparison in candidate metadata.post_filter; the planner promotes that into a real coding_filter step that runs locally over the source step's rows.
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_plan.requestBody.filter_searchText contains RIN
capabilities.example_query: Find RNA samples with a RIN score greater than 7.
capabilities.gap: Only the keyword-anchoring half is observable. The comparison itself lives in ParserCandidate.metadata['post_filter'] = {field, operator, value, value_type}, and agents/parser.py:_candidate_to_parser_plan (line 432) builds the projected ParserPlan WITHOUT passing metadata=, so parser_plan.metadata is always {} in standard mode; the promotion to a coding_filter step (parser.py:859-879) only happens in plan mode, whose PlanStep list never reaches query_complete.debug. Needs parser_plan.metadata.post_filter.operator.

capabilities.name: Truncation / cap / substitution disclosure on any retrieved result
capabilities.description: Computes and carries the flags that tell the chatter how the rows it holds differ from what was asked: rows returned vs page size, API total vs returned rows, LLM-context slimming (5 rows / 5,000 chars), graph LIMIT 5000 caps, and retry-substituted search text. Closes three measured silences: 1,000 of 2,057 reported as 2,057; 5 of 324 assays answered as 'you have access to 5 assays'; undisclosed search-text substitution.
enum_values: row-list keys probed in order: samples, rows, nodes, data
total keys probed in order: total, total_samples, total_nodes (api_row_count also accepts 'count')
api_result_meta: {ok, status_code, url, row_count, bundle_id, total_matching, truncated}
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_result_meta.truncated true
capabilities.example_query: List all the tissue samples in the database.
capabilities.gap: TIS alone exceeds the hard-coded DEFAULT_API_PAGE_SIZE of 1000 (Impact's TIS+CEL is 10,688), so truncated must be True; a False here is the 2026-07-27 'reported the page as the total' regression.

capabilities.name: CC ops: nextseek-parse then nextseek-api-read
capabilities.description: The Container-CC two-stage lookup. nextseek-parse turns a question into a parser plan {mode, target_endpoint, filters} without executing it; nextseek-api-read executes that plan against a 15-path read-safe allowlist and returns rows. --confirmed-write is hard-rejected at the api-read shim with exit 3.
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re \b195\b
capabilities.example_query: That NDMA number looked off to me — can you pull the mouse rows yourself and recount them?
capabilities.gap: Deliberately an outcome on last_reply, the only CC-safe root that can carry an answer: on a container_cc turn every NS outcome field is null by construction (evaluate.py:398). The 'previous answer looked wrong' phrasing is the documented CC trigger, so the case reaches the container without an admin force_route.

groups.name: Tell the truth about capped and substituted results

capabilities.name: Result truncation / substitution flag computation
capabilities.description: Computes the flags telling the chatter and the harness how the rows differ from what was asked: rows returned, page size, whether the API total exceeded the rows, whether context-slimming cut further, and whether the retry ladder substituted a different search string.
enum_values: disclosure: rows_returned, page_size, result_capped, total_matching, preview_rows, search_text_substituted
api_result_meta: ok, status_code, url, row_count, bundle_id, total_matching, truncated
row-list keys probed in order: samples, rows, nodes, data
total keys probed in order: total, total_samples, total_nodes (api_row_count also accepts 'count')
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_result_meta.total_matching gte 1001
capabilities.example_query: List all the tissue samples in the database.
capabilities.gap: Twin of the group-14 disclosure capability; that one asserts the truncated flag, this one asserts the real API total was recovered rather than the 1000-row page being reported as the answer.

capabilities.name: Mandatory chatter disclosure of caps and substitutions
capabilities.description: Prompt-level mandatory rules: report rows_returned not the preview count, describe a capped result as 'the first N of M', and lead with the fact when the user's exact terms returned nothing and the rows shown are for a different search.
enum_values: substitution is called 'the worst failure mode available to you'
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re (?i)(first|showing)\s+[\d,]+\s+of\s+[\d,]+
capabilities.example_query: List all the tissue samples in the database.
capabilities.gap: The prompt mandate is prose ('describe a capped result as the first N of M'), so a phrase match is the honest ceiling. It is still the exact failure that was measured: 1,000 of 2,057 reported as 2,057.

capabilities.name: Graph LIMIT cap must be disclosed
capabilities.description: Record-returning Cypher defaults to LIMIT 5000 as a safety valve; the agent must return the true total alongside rows and a capped result must never be presented as a complete one. Counts are never limited.
enum_values: default record LIMIT 5000 (was 250, which silently truncated ordinary questions)
'A capped result must never be presented as a complete one.'
capabilities.testable_assertion: graph_truncation_disclosed true
capabilities.example_query: List the tissue and cell samples in the Impact study.
capabilities.gap: 10,688 rows against the 5,000 record LIMIT, so the cap definitely fires; the synthetic field (evaluate.py:273) passes only if a real total exceeding the returned rows is also reported.

families.description: Pull the full record for samples the user can already name.

groups.name: Pull the full record for samples I can name

capabilities.name: Full metadata + lineage export for explicit UIDs (admin retrieve)
capabilities.description: Given explicit UIDs, returns complete metadata for those samples plus every parent and child in the lineage, grouped by sample type. Also the metadata source for the reporter pipeline and for pipeline_agent's resolve_samples. Supports an Excel workbook variant.
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re (?i)(parent|child|derived from|lineage)
capabilities.example_query: Give me the full record for sample MUS-200901ENG-23-PUB.
capabilities.gap: Asserts the half of admin retrieve that a plain GET /samples/{uid}/ cannot produce — every parent and child in the lineage, grouped by sample type. Asserting a metadata key instead would need a per-UID ground truth we do not have verified; Scientist/Lab are absent from several sample types (Lab is absent from TIS and D.SEQ entirely).

capabilities.name: CC op: nextseek-sample-search — retrieve visible sample rows by explicit UID
capabilities.description: UID-only read of current sample rows through advanced_search (EXACT match, OR logic, chunked 1,000 UIDs at a time), used to recover the pre-update state of samples. It cannot search by attribute.
enum_values: normalizes json_metadata to dict, parses assay_titles, adds numeric_seek_id
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply mentions MUS-200901ENG-23-PUB
capabilities.example_query: Before I edit it, show me exactly what MUS-200901ENG-23-PUB looks like right now.
capabilities.gap: A UID in the reply can be an echo of the question, so this cannot prove the op ran. What would prove it is which CC op was invoked. That data exists per turn as cc_traces, written by nextseek_api/cc_assistant/cc_turn_complete.py into the session chat_log, but query_complete emits only {reply, mode, artifacts, cc_raw_files} and chat_log.* is blocked at evaluate.py:372. Needs a cc_traces.ops field on query_complete.

families.description: List the platform's own objects: assays, projects, people, protocols, investigations.

groups.name: Browse the platform: assays, projects, people, protocols, investigations

capabilities.name: SEEK platform listings (assays, projects, people, SOPs, investigations, data files, sample types, schema)
capabilities.description: The read-only GET family: list or fetch-by-id the platform's organizational records plus the OpenAPI schema and a sample type's distinct child types. These are SEEK JSON:API passthroughs, some of which carry no `total` — the reason result disclosure exists (a 324-row assay listing was answered as 'you have access to 5 assays').
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re \b324\b
capabilities.example_query: What assays do I have access to?
capabilities.gap: 324 is the verified accessible-assay row count and the exact case that produced 'you have access to 5 assays' when only the 5-row LLM preview reached the chatter — so a wrong answer here is the disclosure defect, visible.

capabilities.name: Routable REST endpoint catalog (10 enriched entries)
capabilities.description: The endpoint set the parser and api_agent actually route to, each carrying description, category, requires_uids, supports_free_text, primary_entities, intent_patterns, an llm_hint, example_intents and a request_body template. This is the effective read surface of the REST corridor. The CC plugin ships a parallel copy with 13 entries.
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_plan.endpoint eq /nextseek_api/people/
capabilities.example_query: Who are the researchers registered in NExtSEEK?
capabilities.gap: Tests the catalog's operative rule — pick the most specific enriched entry, advanced_search is the last-resort catch-all. eq rather than contains so falling back to the catch-all fails.

capabilities.name: Full REST endpoint catalog (40 paths, incl. write verbs)
capabilities.description: The complete 40-endpoint catalog including POST/PATCH/DELETE. Not loaded by chat_nextseek at runtime (grep finds zero references) — it ships only to the Container-CC nextseek plugin, which is the surface that can actually write.
capabilities.testable_assertion: not expressible — build-time image asset, reachable_from_chat=no
capabilities.example_query: What endpoints can you write to?
capabilities.gap: The atlas itself records reachable_from_chat=no and grep finds zero runtime references from chat_nextseek; the file ships only into the CC image at docker/cc-runtime/build_context/plugins/nextseek/context/min_api_endpoints.json. Nothing in a chat turn observes which catalog file the agent read. This belongs in the container lane (nessie_tests/tests_container/) as a file-presence assertion, not in the HTTP corpus — the Dockerfile already fails the build if min_*.json is absent, which is the stronger guarantee.

families.description: Structural questions over the graph, including every assay and protocol traversal.

groups.name: Answer structural questions by traversing the graph

capabilities.name: Generate and run Cypher over the sample/study/investigation graph (mode=graph_query)
capabilities.description: Converts a structural question into parameterized Cypher using the live graph schema, plus a protocol vocabulary and an assay-to-parent/child table injected only when the question mentions those domains. The orchestrator runs it and retries exactly once with the verbatim Neo4j error on failure. Sample nodes carry only uuid/type/id, so no keyword, tissue or treatment filtering is possible on this path.
enum_values: node:Sample (properties uuid, type, id — and ONLY these three)
node:SampleType (no `code` property — filtering it always yields 0)
rel:DERIVED_FROM (child)->(parent), carries internal_assay_title, internal_assay_id, protocol_title, protocol_id, child_id, parent_id
derivation chain vocabulary: D.SEQ -> DNA -> TIS -> PAV -> NHP
conditional context: PROTOCOL VOCABULARY when query matches protocol|method|procedure|technique
conditional context: ASSAY-SAMPLE CONNECTIONS when query matches assay|sequencing|cytometry|spectrometry|imaging|data|processed|associated|underwent|via|collection|extraction
retry: exactly one, with retry_context = the verbatim Neo4j error
artifact: graph_debug_<ts>.json with a 20-row data preview
failure mode: neo4j driver not installed
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re \b705\b
capabilities.example_query: How many mice are in the Impact study?

capabilities.name: The closed set of Cypher shapes this door can issue
capabilities.description: The graph_agent is constrained by prompt to a small closed set of shapes and the report runners hard-code two more. Knowing these bounds what a graph answer can possibly be. Three shapes are explicitly banned because each produced a measured wrong answer.
enum_values: Study/Investigation scope disjunction: MATCH (s:Sample)-[:IN_STUDY]->(st:Study) WHERE toLower(st.title) CONTAINS toLower($project) OR EXISTS { MATCH (st)-[:IN_INVESTIGATION]->(inv:Investigation) WHERE toLower(inv.title) CONTAINS toLower($project) }
Sample-type filter: WHERE s.type = $type (never traverse OF_TYPE to SampleType)
Assay direct participant (Case 1, single-hop): WHERE (a.type=$type OR b.type=$type) AND r.internal_assay_title=$assay … LIMIT 5000
Assay indirect/ancestor (Case 2): assay edge single-hop then (assay_parent)-[:DERIVED_FROM*0..]->(ancestor) WHERE ancestor.type=$ancestor_type … LIMIT 5000
AND-across-descendant-types: MATCH (c)-[:DERIVED_FROM*1..]->(p) WITH p, collect(DISTINCT c.type) AS matched_types WHERE size(matched_types)=size(child_types)
Scoped count: RETURN count(s) AS total (never LIMITed)
Breakdown by project: RETURN inv.title AS project, count(DISTINCT s) AS sample_count ORDER BY sample_count DESC

Report runner: MATCH (inv:Investigation)<-[:IN_INVESTIGATION]-(study:Study)<-[:IN_STUDY]-(s:Sample) WHERE toLower(inv.title)=toLower($inv_title) [+ substring(split(s.uuid,'-')[1],0,2) IN $yy_list] RETURN DISTINCT s.uuid
Report runner (published): same traversal with replace(toLower(inv.title),' ','') CONTAINS $proj_hint RETURN s.uuid, study.title, s.type
Standard record columns: s.uuid AS uuid, s.id AS id, s.type AS type
BANNED: OPTIONAL MATCH followed by a bare WHERE — silently discards the filter, returned 50,161 (every sample in any study) instead of 705
BANNED: relationship properties on a variable-length path [r:DERIVED_FROM*1..] (type error)
BANNED: filtering SampleType.code — the property does not exist, always 0 results
capabilities.testable_assertion: graph_cypher matches_re \.type\s*=
capabilities.example_query: How many NHP samples are in the SRP investigation?
capabilities.gap: The mandated sample-type filter is WHERE s.type = $type; traversing OF_TYPE to SampleType is the banned shape and always yields 0 because SampleType has no code property.

capabilities.name: Neo4j read-only Cypher tool (the graph data door)
capabilities.description: Executes parameterised Cypher against the graph, opening and closing a driver per call, and returns records plus count, true total, a truncated flag and the effective limit.
enum_values: success: {ok:true, data:[dict], count, total, truncated, limit, cypher, parameters, counters}
capabilities.testable_assertion: graph_result.count eq 10
capabilities.example_query: List the studies in MetNet.
capabilities.gap: MetNet has exactly 10 studies (verified). Record-returning phrasing so count is the row count, not 1.

capabilities.name: True-total probe for LIMIT-capped graph results
capabilities.description: When a graph query returns exactly as many rows as its trailing LIMIT, re-runs the body wrapped in CALL () { … } RETURN count(*) to get the real total, and reports {count, total, truncated, limit} rather than passing the cap off as the answer. Handles literal and parameter-bound limits; a failed probe yields total=None.
enum_values: probe wrap: CALL () { <body> } RETURN count(*) AS __total
matches an optional SKIP n then LIMIT (\d+|$\w+)
capabilities.testable_assertion: graph_result.total gte 10000
capabilities.example_query: List the tissue and cell samples in the Impact study.
capabilities.gap: 10,688 rows against LIMIT 5000 forces the CALL () { … } RETURN count(*) probe; a failed probe yields total=None and fails this.

capabilities.name: Ambiguous 'study X' resolved as Study.title OR Investigation.title
capabilities.description: Any named study/project/cohort scope is matched case-insensitively against BOTH node types as a disjunction using EXISTS { }, because short project names live on Investigation while Study.title values are usually full publication titles. 'NHP samples from study IMPACT' returns hundreds via Investigation.title and zero via Study.title alone.
enum_values: forbidden form: OPTIONAL MATCH + bare WHERE (returns 50,161 for any $project; correct answer for Impact is 705)
capabilities.testable_assertion: graph_cypher matches_re EXISTS\s*\{
capabilities.example_query: How many NHP samples are in the study called Impact?
capabilities.gap: Short project names live on Investigation while Study.title holds full publication titles, so the disjunction is mandatory; the forbidden OPTIONAL MATCH + bare WHERE form returned 50,161 for every $project.

capabilities.name: Guard: rewrite <var>.UID reads to the canonical <var>.uuid
capabilities.description: The cached schema advertises both uuid and UID on Sample; handed that, the model sometimes filters on .UID, matches nothing and reports a confident negative. Runs first, on the masked Cypher so .UID inside a string literal is untouched, and appends a '[uid guard: …]' note to the explanation.
capabilities.testable_assertion: graph_result.count gte 1
capabilities.example_query: Are MUS-200901ENG-23-PUB and D.SEQ-221031SHA-67 related to each other?
capabilities.gap: The guard's failure mode is a confident false zero: filtering on .UID (advertised by the cached schema but never populated) matches nothing. A UID-anchored graph question returning zero rows IS the unrewritten query. Asserting on graph_cypher instead would pass trivially, since the standard record columns already contain s.uuid.

capabilities.name: Guard: reject and re-prompt Cypher filtering on non-existent properties
capabilities.description: Scans for <var>.<Prop> reads that appear on no node label and no relationship type (a hallucinated s.Lab), re-prompts once with the offending list plus the valid property set, and returns an empty plan if the repair still references unknown properties. Runs on the MASKED Cypher because an inlined literal like WHERE s.type = D.SEQ otherwise reads as a property access on a variable named D.
capabilities.testable_assertion: graph_cypher matches_re (?s)^(?!.*\.Lab\b)
capabilities.example_query: Which samples in the Impact study come from the Essigmann lab?
capabilities.gap: Lab is the perfect trap: it is a real json_metadata key on 5,715 samples but is NOT a graph property, so s.Lab is exactly the hallucinated access the guard exists to catch. Verified the regex: matches '…RETURN s.uuid, s.label' (passes) and fails on 'WHERE s.Lab = …'. (?s) is needed because Cypher is multi-line and matches_re applies IGNORECASE.

capabilities.name: Guard: insert the missing WITH before a leaked OPTIONAL MATCH filter
capabilities.description: A WHERE written directly after an OPTIONAL MATCH joins the optional pattern instead of filtering rows, so the filter is silently discarded. Detects the case (the WHERE touches a variable bound before the OPTIONAL MATCH) and injects WITH <all bound vars>. Measured: 50,161 rows without the WITH, 705 with it; the model drops it roughly 40% of the time. Fails soft, and runs last so it also covers Cypher produced by the property repair.
capabilities.testable_assertion: graph_result.count eq 705
capabilities.example_query: List the mouse samples in the Impact study.
capabilities.gap: This is the measured pair: 50,161 rows without the WITH, 705 with it, and the model drops it about 40% of the time. 705 is under the 5,000 LIMIT so count is exact and unambiguous.

capabilities.name: Known investigation / study scope vocabulary
capabilities.description: The named organizational scopes users can query against, and the strongest single signal for graph_query routing. The value set genuinely differs per instance and per source file — three different lists exist in the tree (neo4j_schema.json has 6, _dev has 7 incl. BreakThroughCancer, _prod has a different 7).
enum_values: GBM_BTC — Glioblastoma / Brain Tumor Center combined program
GBM — a Study inside Break Through Cancer, not an Investigation
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply mentions MetNet
capabilities.example_query: What investigations exist in the database?
capabilities.gap: 6 investigations are verified (CSBC, Griffith, Impact, MetNet, SRP, Shoulders). MetNet is present in all three schema files in the tree, so it survives the per-instance drift the atlas warns about; GBM deliberately not used, it exists nowhere.

capabilities.name: Protocol title vocabulary carried on DERIVED_FROM
capabilities.description: The controlled protocol vocabulary on DERIVED_FROM.protocol_title, used to answer 'associated with X protocol' questions REST cannot express. The agent fuzzy-matches the user's term against the vocabulary and falls back to CONTAINS.
capabilities.testable_assertion: graph_cypher contains protocol_title
capabilities.example_query: Which samples were collected using the tissue collection protocol?
capabilities.gap: The PROTOCOL VOCABULARY context block is injected only when the question matches protocol|method|procedure|technique, so the query wording is load-bearing; REST cannot express this question at all.

capabilities.name: Assay to parent_type/child_type connection map
capabilities.description: Maps each assay to the parent and child sample types it connects; the graph agent consults it to choose between a direct-participant single-hop query and an indirect ancestor multi-hop query.
enum_values: Case 2 — indirect / ancestor (single-hop assay edge + DERIVED_FROM*0..)
capabilities.testable_assertion: graph_result.count eq 139
capabilities.example_query: Which monkeys have sequencing data? List them.
capabilities.gap: The single best discriminator in the whole block: 139 NHP animals have a D.SEQ descendant (the Case-2 ancestor multi-hop), 1,608 is the D.SEQ-side reading, and 408 is every NHP sample — the live regression this harness caught on 2026-07-28. All three are distinguishable by one number.

capabilities.name: Graph-vs-REST-vs-reporter disambiguation table
capabilities.description: A machine-readable trigger table shipped alongside the routing prompt as GRAPH_SCHEMA: 6 graph_query triggers, 5 api_preferred triggers and 8 disambiguation rules, the last of which lists the recognizable investigation titles. The decisive test is whether answering requires a relationship hop (IN_STUDY / IN_INVESTIGATION / DERIVED_FROM).
capabilities.testable_assertion: parser_plan.mode eq graph_query
capabilities.example_query: Which mice are in the Impact study?
capabilities.gap: The table's decisive test is whether answering needs a relationship hop (IN_STUDY / IN_INVESTIGATION / DERIVED_FROM). Study membership does; a REST route here is a false zero, since a child record does not contain its study as text.

families.description: Trace what came from what, in either direction.

groups.name: Trace what came from what

capabilities.name: Lineage / derivation tree for ONE named UID
capabilities.description: GET the bidirectional derivation graph for one sample: what it came from and what was derived from it, as graph-friendly nodes/edges. Node-only — the catalog explicitly redirects full metadata export to admin/samples/retrieve/.
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_plan.endpoint contains sample-tree
capabilities.example_query: What was sample MUS-200901ENG-23-PUB derived from?
capabilities.gap: An outcome assertion would have to name the parent UID, and no per-UID lineage ground truth is verified. The endpoint choice is still diagnostic: the catalog explicitly redirects full-metadata asks away from the tree endpoint and vice versa, and a single-UID lineage question landing on advanced_search is the documented false-zero path.

capabilities.name: UID-count discriminator: 1 UID stays on REST, 2+ forces the graph
capabilities.description: A lineage question anchored on ONE UID is REST work (sample-tree / retrieve), but TWO OR MORE UIDs deterministically re-routes to graph_query with every UID in filters.uids — because a child record does not contain its parent's UID as text, so advanced_search returns a convincing false zero. A plain record lookup ('full details for X and Y') is exempted.
enum_values: >=2 UIDs -> graph_query with all UIDs in filters.uids
capabilities.testable_assertion: parser_plan.mode eq graph_query
capabilities.example_query: Are MUS-200901ENG-23-PUB and D.SEQ-221031SHA-67 related?
capabilities.gap: _MIN_UIDS_FOR_FORCED_GRAPH = 2 and both UIDs match the well-formed regex; the question carries a relation phrase so the 'full details for X and Y' record-lookup exemption does not apply. Anything but graph_query means advanced_search will return a convincing false zero.

capabilities.name: Find parent samples having descendants of ALL named child types
capabilities.description: AND-logic across child sample types: returns the source samples (animals, patients) that have derived samples of every requested type, optionally narrowed by parent type (OR). This is how 'monkeys with both imaging and sequencing' is answered without the graph. The body may contain ONLY the two array fields.
enum_values: child_sample_types: logical AND across the list (array, never an object)
parent_sample_type_filters: logical OR across the list (array, never an object)
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_plan.endpoint contains parents_by_child_types
capabilities.example_query: Which monkeys have both imaging and sequencing data?
capabilities.gap: This is the only endpoint that does AND-logic across child sample types; advanced_search would OR them and over-return. No verified row count for the AND intersection, so the endpoint is the strongest concrete assertion available.

capabilities.name: Enumerate the data leaves under a lineage bundle
capabilities.description: Walks a retrieved metadata bundle (roots plus nested children) and returns every sample whose sample_type is in an accepted set, carrying the root UID it was reached from so the caller can report 'N source UIDs have zero matching leaves'. Handles both the one-level fixture shape and the real doubly-wrapped API body.
enum_values: accepted_leaf_sample_types for the accession/fetchngs path: [] (short-circuits, lineage not walked)
assay read from metadata['assay_name'], fallbacks 'assay' then 'AssayName'
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_artifact.samplesheet.csv.rows_gte gte 4
capabilities.example_query: Run RNA-seq on the sequencing samples under D.SEQ-240910LAU.
capabilities.gap: The leaf walk is only visible through its downstream product, so this cannot separate a leaf-enumeration bug from a samplesheet-writing bug, and it silently caps at MAX_RESOLVE_LEAVES=75. The direct observable — how many D.SEQ leaves were reached and how many root UIDs yielded zero — is computed by helpers/lineage.py:enumerate_lineage_leaves and stored only in the pipeline_agent session block, which is blocked at evaluate.py:372. Needs a leaf count surfaced on query_complete. (4 is the verified D.SEQ-240910LAU sample count from the green Luria run.)

families.description: Turn the user's words into NExtSEEK codes before anything else runs.

groups.name: Turn what I said into NExtSEEK's vocabulary

capabilities.name: Resolve a question into sample types, assays, keywords, projects and lab codes
capabilities.description: First agent of every NS turn and the CC equivalent op. Converts free text into catalog-closed vocabulary across six buckets; lab_codes are filled deterministically after the LLM. Its output is copied VERBATIM into ParserPlan.resolved by hard rule. Three-tier failure handling: structured call, one structured retry on timeout, a raw chat fallback under a 180s guard, then an empty output.
enum_values: bucket: assays (list of {code, name}; assays have no separate code — Name is used for both)
bucket: lab_codes (never emitted by the LLM; filled deterministically downstream)
capabilities.testable_assertion: entity_sampletype_codes contains MUS
capabilities.example_query: Find me mice treated with NDMA.
capabilities.gap: contains on a list is exact element membership (e2e/criteria.py:219), so this is an exact code assertion, not a substring.

capabilities.name: Site-specific mapping conventions that override general biology
capabilities.description: Hardcoded mappings reflecting how this specific lab stores samples, which explicitly override general biological reasoning. PBMC is a TIS with a retained keyword, not a CEL and not an assay.
enum_values: PBMC / PBMCs / peripheral blood mononuclear cells -> TIS + keyword PBMC (never CEL, never an assay)
BAL / bronchoalveolar lavage -> TIS + keyword BAL
T cell, NK cell, natural killer cell, macrophage, monocyte, dendritic cell, neutrophil, B cell -> CEL + keyword
NHP / non-human primate / macaque / monkey -> NHP
capabilities.testable_assertion: entity_sampletype_codes contains TIS
capabilities.example_query: How many PBMC samples do we have?
capabilities.gap: PBMC -> TIS + keyword PBMC is the flagship hardcoded override: general biology says CEL, and CEL here is the documented wrong answer.

capabilities.name: D.* raw vs A.* analyzed sample-type selection
capabilities.description: 'analyzed' / 'analysis' / 'processed' / 'results' is a sample type SELECTOR, never a keyword: it switches emission from the D.* raw types to the A.* analysis types. No sample has the literal word 'analyzed' in its metadata, so D.SEQ + keyword 'analyzed' returns zero rows — which is what used to happen.
enum_values: analyzed sequencing -> A.GEX, A.ALN, A.VCF, A.CNV, A.SCXP (also A.SCCL, A.CHRM, A.DBMM)
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_plan.requestBody.filter_searchText matches_re (?s)^(?!.*analyz)
capabilities.example_query: Show me the analyzed sequencing results.
capabilities.gap: Asserts the negative that the rule is about: 'analyzed' is a sample-type SELECTOR, never a keyword, because no sample carries the literal word — D.SEQ + keyword 'analyzed' returned zero rows, which is exactly what used to happen. Regex verified against 'D.SEQ analyzed' (fails) and 'sequencing' (passes). Asserting entity_sampletype_codes contains A.GEX would be brittle: any of A.GEX/A.ALN/A.VCF/A.CNV/A.SCXP is a correct emission.

capabilities.name: Shortlist the sample-type and assay catalogs for the entity prompt
capabilities.description: Reduces the 101 sample types and 217 assays to the plausibly relevant subset so the prompt stays small. Three paths: legacy rapidfuzz-only top-K; a hybrid of lexical + semantic + code-hit fused with RRF and cut dynamically; and an automatic fall-through to legacy on any hybrid failure with the reason recorded. Exact code hits are always included regardless of score.
enum_values: path 1: legacy rapidfuzz-only (no/unready indexes), diagnostics.enabled = False
path 2: hybrid lexical + semantic + code-hit fused with RRF, diagnostics.enabled = True
path 3: hybrid failure -> legacy, diagnostics.fallback_reason = 'hybrid path failure: <Type>: <msg>'
code_bonus: +35.0 substring hit in the normalized query
capabilities.testable_assertion: shortlist_sampletype_codes contains D.SEQ
capabilities.example_query: How many D.SEQ samples were uploaded last year?
capabilities.gap: Tests the one invariant that holds on ALL THREE shortlist paths (legacy, hybrid, hybrid-failure fallback): an exact code hit is always included regardless of score. shortlist_sampletype_codes is an existing alias at e2e/criteria.py:182.

capabilities.name: Cached embedding index over a catalog (SemanticIndex)
capabilities.description: Embeds a catalog once with sentence-transformers, L2-normalises, persists the matrix to an .npz keyed by sha256 of the catalog JSON, and answers cosine top-N queries. Rebuilds when the catalog or model changes. Every failure mode degrades to ready=False with a fail_reason and callers fall back to lexical-only. Three named indexes exist, all off by default.
enum_values: index name: sampletypes (catalog FULL_SAMPLETYPES, id SampleType, doc_sampletype)
index name: assays (catalog FULL_ASSAYS, id Name, doc_assay)
index name: endpoints (catalog MIN_API_ENDPOINTS, id path, doc_endpoint)
capabilities.testable_assertion: shortlist_diagnostics.enabled true
capabilities.example_query: Find PBMCs that were sequenced using single cell methods.
capabilities.gap: Requires requires_env SEMANTIC_SHORTLIST_ENABLED=1 (default False). enabled=True is set at catalog_match.py:155 ONLY on the hybrid path, so it is False on both legacy paths and on any index failure — exactly the ready=False degradation the capability claims. Resolves today via the dot-notation fallback off debug['shortlist_diagnostics'] (orchestrator.py:685); no evaluator work needed, it is just a field root the corpus has never used.

capabilities.name: Reciprocal Rank Fusion and score-ratio dynamic top-K
capabilities.description: fuse_rrf merges any number of ranked lists by summing 1/(k+rank) per item id so an item ranked well by two rankers beats an item ranked first by only one. dynamic_cutoff then keeps every candidate scoring at least ratio * top_score, clamped between min_k and max_k, so an unambiguous query returns 3 candidates and an ambiguous one returns 80.
enum_values: min_k fallback when the top score is 0
capabilities.testable_assertion: shortlist_diagnostics.sampletype_ranks nonempty
capabilities.example_query: Find PBMCs that were sequenced using single cell methods.
capabilities.gap: Also requires SEMANTIC_SHORTLIST_ENABLED=1. sampletype_ranks is populated only from _hybrid_shortlist's fused ranking (catalog_match.py:151) and stays {} on every legacy path, so non-empty means RRF actually ran. It does not check the ratio-0.7 cutoff arithmetic — that is genuinely unit-lane work on fuse_rrf/dynamic_cutoff.

capabilities.name: Embeddable-text builders for sampletypes, assays and endpoints
capabilities.description: Decide which catalog fields get embedded. Curated deliberately: sampletype docs add Clade, parent/child types and associated assay parents/children so 'PBMCs sequenced via single cell' surfaces TIS, while excluding metadata field-NAME noise and any field past the model's 512-token cap. Endpoint docs lean on intent_patterns and example_intents.
enum_values: doc_sampletype fields: SampleType, Name, Clade, Tags, Parent_SampleTypes, Child_SampleTypes, Associated Assay Parents, Associated Assay Children, Description

doc_assay fields: Name, Alternative Assay Names/alternative_assay_names, Tags, Critical Attributes, AssociatedRepository, Parent Clade Type, Child Clade Type, Required Parent Sample Types, Optional Parent Sample Types, Children Sample Types, Description
doc_endpoint fields: path, category, description, intent_patterns, example_intents, llm_hint
excluded from sampletype docs: Required/Standard Metadata (field NAMES, ~60 tokens of noise)
excluded from sampletype docs: Possible Metadata Fields (>600 tokens, past the 512-token cap)
excluded from assay docs: Protocols_UIDs, Protocols_Phrases
capabilities.testable_assertion: not expressible — pure build-time functions with no per-turn observable
capabilities.example_query: Find PBMCs that were sequenced using single cell methods.
capabilities.gap: doc_sampletype/doc_assay/doc_endpoint decide which catalog FIELDS get embedded. Their output is text fed to sentence-transformers at index-build time; nothing per-turn records which fields were included, and the curation decisions being asserted (Clade in, Required/Standard Metadata out, >512-token fields out) are only checkable by inspecting the produced document string. This is a unit test over catalog_semantic.doc_* , not a corpus case. No evaluator field would fix it.

capabilities.name: Project name/id normalization with fuzzy fallback
capabilities.description: Turns a project reference (int, numeric string or name) into the canonical SEEK project id via the DB-loaded PROJECT_NAME_TO_ID map, with a containment-based fuzzy fallback that logs a warning when it fires, and a ValueError listing the valid keys when nothing matches — a real error rather than a silently wrong scope.
capabilities.testable_assertion: reporter_plan.project eq MetNet
capabilities.example_query: How many samples did metnet upload last year?
capabilities.gap: Lower-cased in the query on purpose so the containment fuzzy fallback is what has to fire; eq (not matches_re) so a wrong-but-plausible scope fails rather than passing on a case-insensitive near miss.

capabilities.name: Automatic vocabulary resolution on every CC prompt (UserPromptSubmit hook)
capabilities.description: Before the agent acts on any prompt, entity-extract runs outside the agent's control and injects the resolved {sampletypes, assays, keywords, projects} as additionalContext, so abbreviations are expanded and op calls are grounded. Fail-open: missing prompt, missing bin, timeout or malformed result emits nothing. Re-registered into ~/.claude/settings.json at container start because the headless runtime does not load plugin hooks.json.
enum_values: output prefix: 'NExtSEEK vocabulary auto-resolved for this query…'
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply mentions TIS
capabilities.example_query: I need to put together an upload sheet for our PBMC samples — what am I working with?
capabilities.gap: Only the hook's downstream effect is visible: if PBMC was expanded to TIS before the agent acted, the answer talks about TIS. The hook's own additionalContext block (prefix 'NExtSEEK vocabulary auto-resolved for this query…', emitted by plugins/nextseek/hooks/entity_preamble.sh) never leaves the container — it goes to the agent's stdin and to outputs/<ts>/console.txt, and query_complete carries no field for it. Fail-open is the killer: a missing bin or a 25s timeout emits nothing and the agent may still answer 'TIS' from the baked catalog, so this cannot distinguish hook-fired from hook-silent. Needs a cc_hook_context field.

capabilities.name: CC op: nextseek-sampletype-attrs — fetch a sample type's attribute schema
capabilities.description: Returns the structured attribute definitions for a sample type (title, required, is_title, …) so rows are populated against the real schema rather than invented fields; --list returns the whole sample-type catalog.
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply mentions Genotype
capabilities.example_query: I'm building an upload sheet for mouse samples — what attributes does that sample type need?
capabilities.gap: Genotype is a verified live MUS attribute (histogram RG 44 / RGATG 39 / RGA 30 …), so it comes back only from the real GET /sample_types/{ref}/ attribute schema, not from invention. CC-safe root.

capabilities.name: CC ops: nextseek-assay-resolve and nextseek-project-resolve
capabilities.description: Live, fail-closed resolution of curator-supplied names to ids. Assay titles resolve against the accessible assay map narrowed by the selected project, raising on ambiguity or zero matches. Project resolution is two-phase (show, then --confirmed) against the live /projects/ API, never auto-selects even when exactly one project exists, and never trusts the cached projects_db.json.
enum_values: project token: {project_id, resolved_title, confirmed, accessible_project_ids, accessible_projects}
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re (?i)(confirm|which project|is that the right project)
capabilities.example_query: Which project should I upload these into?
capabilities.gap: Asserts the fail-closed rule, not the lookup: project resolution is two-phase and must NEVER auto-select even when exactly one project exists — and exactly one does here ('Published Data', verified). A reply that just names it, with no confirmation step, is the defect.

capabilities.name: CC route: reconcile a 'study' name across stores
capabilities.description: 'Study' is not one thing: it can be an Investigation node, a Study node (usually a publication title), or merely a metadata attribute on the samples. Only the third case routes to the container. Worked example in the registry: '4 week' is not a node at all, it is a Cohort value on NHP records (2 samples as '4 week', 237 more as '4wk').
enum_values: case (a) an Investigation node — handled by nextseek_query
case (b) a Study node, usually a full publication title — handled by nextseek_query
case (c) only a metadata attribute on the samples — the ONLY case that routes here
trigger (i): the user says a previous study answer looked wrong, empty or suspicious
trigger (ii): the scope reads like a descriptive cohort/condition/timepoint label and is not a known graph name
known investigations named in the registry: CSBC, Griffith, Impact, MetNet, SRP, Shoulders
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re \b(237|239)\b
capabilities.example_query: How many NHP samples are in the 4 week study? The last answer looked wrong.
capabilities.gap: The registry's own worked example, with verified numbers: '4 week' is not a node at all, it is a Cohort value — 2 rows spelled '4 week' and 237 spelled '4wk'. Only an actual cross-store reconciliation reaches 237 or the 239 union; a graph-node lookup returns 0 and the un-reconciled REST answer returns 2.

families.description: What the system is, what it can do, what vocabulary exists.

groups.name: Ask what the system is and what vocabulary exists

capabilities.name: Question about the system itself (mode=system_question)
capabilities.description: Answers capability, catalog-entity and search-option questions from the capabilities doc and catalogs without touching REST or the graph. The agent picks its own sub-mode, hydrates full catalog records for whatever the entity agent resolved, and returns finished markdown the orchestrator displays verbatim. No result bundle is created (bundle_id is None), which is why these turns are not refinable.
enum_values: mode=get_capabilities — what the system can do in general; drawn from CAPABILITIES_DOCUMENT
mode=get_entities — a specific catalog item; drawn exclusively from ENTITY_DETAILS, falls back to get_capabilities when ENTITY_DETAILS is empty
mode=get_searches — what search surfaces / endpoints / graph relationships exist; drawn from ENDPOINT_CATALOG and GRAPH_SCHEMA
router sub-intent (a) what a named catalog entity IS — assay, sample type, project, study, protocol
router sub-intent (b) what the system can DO and who the caller IS — capabilities, search-mode differences, identity, session, access scope
router sub-intent (c) what EXISTS as options — assays, sample types, endpoints, graph relationships
router sub-intent (d) how the catalog is SHAPED — frequency, distribution, counts by category, most/least common
output: {mode, narrative (markdown, shown as-is), entities_consulted[], notes}
capabilities.testable_assertion: parser_plan.mode eq system_question
capabilities.example_query: What can you help me with?
capabilities.gap: The mode IS the capability, and it is the only assertion available: these turns touch neither REST nor the graph and create no bundle (bundle_id None), so api_result_meta and graph_result are both absent and every outcome field is False by construction. Do not add an outcome floor to this family.

capabilities.name: Sample type catalog (101 codes)
capabilities.description: The complete controlled vocabulary of sample type codes the system can filter, query and ground against, spanning organism (MUS, NHP, PAT), biological (TIS, CEL, DNA, RNA), data (D.*) and analysis (A.*) families. Cached as JSON in context/, refreshable from MySQL, and baked into the CC image.
enum_values: per-item fields: SampleType, ID, Name, Description, Tags, Required Metadata, Standard Metadata, Possible Metadata Fields, Clade, Associated Assay Parents, Associated Assay Children, Parent_SampleTypes, Child_SampleTypes
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re \b101\b
capabilities.example_query: How many sample types are there?

capabilities.name: Assay catalog (217 entries)
capabilities.description: The controlled vocabulary of experimental processes. Assays have no separate code — the Name is used for both code and name. In the graph they live as DERIVED_FROM.internal_assay_title (88-93 distinct titles depending on instance). The enum below is the deduplicated primary set of the 217 rows; many entries additionally have '<X> Analysis' companions and long-form aliases.
enum_values: (217 rows total; the above is the deduplicated primary set)

per-item fields: Name, Description, Tags, Alternative Assay Names, Required/Optional Parent Sample Types, Children Sample Types, Parent/Child Clade Type, AssaySheet Link, AssociatedRepository, Critical Attributes, Protocols_Phrases, Protocols_UIDs, Internal Assay ID
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re \b217\b
capabilities.example_query: How many different assay types does NExtSEEK have in its catalog?
capabilities.gap: Query wording deliberately says 'in its catalog' — 217 is the catalog row count, 324 is the accessible-assay LISTING count from GET /assays/, and asking loosely ('how many assays are there') legitimately admits either. Case authors must keep the wording.

capabilities.name: CC baked reference catalogs — answer vocabulary questions with zero network
capabilities.description: Nine read-only catalogs baked into the agent image that answer 'what sample types exist', 'what assays are there', 'what can I ask', 'which endpoints exist', 'what does the graph hold' directly with the Read tool — no op call, no credentials. The Dockerfile fails the build if the min_*.json catalogs are absent.
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re \b101\b
capabilities.example_query: While you're in there, remind me how many sample types NExtSEEK defines.
capabilities.gap: Gets the answer but not the claim. 'Zero network, no op call, no credentials' is the whole point of the baked catalogs, and nothing in query_complete distinguishes a Read of min_sampletypes_db.json from a live GET /sample_types/ — both produce 101. Needs the same cc_traces.ops field as the other CC-op capabilities; the tool-use record exists inside the container and is dropped at the boundary.

families.description: Ask about results already returned, including aggregating an attribute over 'those'. Absorbs within-chat memory for both engines.

groups.name: Ask a follow-up about results I already have

capabilities.name: Follow-up over already-returned results (mode=ask_about_last_results)
capabilities.description: Answers a question about data already retrieved this session without re-querying. Resolves which stored bundle the user means, runs the memory agent over that bundle's full payload, and re-surfaces that bundle's files and debug panel. The memory prompt forbids calling or assuming any external database.
enum_values: outcome: no results_history -> 'there are no stored results in this session yet'
outcome: named id not found -> "I couldn't find that in this session"
planner alias: memory_lookup and ask_about_last_results are functionally identical, only the reported tool name differs
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_result_meta.source_mode eq new_search
capabilities.example_query: How many of those are RG genotype?
capabilities.gap: Two-turn case, turn 1 'Find me mice treated with NDMA'. source_mode is set ONLY on the memory branch (orchestrator.py:777) and carries the mode of the bundle being read, so it proves the turn answered from a stored bundle instead of re-querying — the memory prompt forbids touching any external database. Also the branch evaluate.py:235 relies on to keep such a turn from a false floor failure.

capabilities.name: Select WHICH prior result bundle a follow-up refers to
capabilities.description: Three layers: the parser picks target_result_id from the visible window (newest by default, oldest for 'the first search'/'originally'/'earliest', or the bundle whose query mentions a named entity); when it cannot, resolve_bundle_for_recall scores every bundle by significant-word overlap so 'the first search' does not silently resolve to the newest; the planner variant additionally accepts explicit metadata keys.
enum_values: target_result_id = null + notes 'bundle not in visible window — memory agent should look it up by content'
recall word pattern \b[\w.-]{2,}\b preserves dots/dashes so D.SEQ, NDMA, MUS-200901ENG-23-PUB survive
planner metadata bundle-id keys: target_result_id, refers_to_result_id, result_id, bundle_id
planner metadata query keys: target_query, prior_query, original_query, refers_to_query
planner latest-bundle trigger tokens: 'last result', 'latest result', 'previous result', 'those results', 'that search'
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_target_result_id eq 1
capabilities.example_query: Going back to my first search — how many were there?
capabilities.gap: Three-turn case: NDMA mice (bundle 1), CD8 antibodies (bundle 2), then this. 'the first search' is an explicit oldest-trigger phrase, so resolving to 2 is the exact silent-newest bug the three-layer resolution exists to prevent. last_target_result_id is an existing alias (e2e/criteria.py:174) for parser_plan.target_result_id.

capabilities.name: Compute the follow-up answer with sandboxed generated Python
capabilities.description: The fast path: pick the best JSON payload out of the prior bundle, profile its shape, ask the memory_coder for a short Python snippet, execute it in an AST-validated subset under a 3-second SIGALRM, save a timestamped artifact, and have the chatter phrase the computed result. The prompt mandates exact field comparison over substring scans (a substring 'SHA' matched URL fragments inside HTML-wrapped UIDs) and prefers 'I do not have that field' over guessing.
enum_values: pre-bound names: data, rows, re, json, strip_html, result
allowed builtins: len, str, int, float, bool, list, dict, set, tuple, sorted, sum, min, max, any, all, enumerate, range, isinstance
allowed exception classes: Exception, ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, AttributeError
allowed methods: get, items, keys, values, append, extend, add, update, lower, upper, strip, split, replace, startswith, endswith, isdigit, join
allowed re methods: search, match, fullmatch, findall, sub
allowed control flow: if/elif/else, for, comprehensions, try/except
blocked AST nodes: Import, ImportFrom, FunctionDef, AsyncFunctionDef, ClassDef, Lambda, With, AsyncWith, Delete, Global, Nonlocal, Raise, While, Await, Yield, YieldFrom
blocked names: eval, exec, compile, open, __import__, globals, locals, vars, dir, help, input, print
blocked: any dunder attribute access or dunder method call
blocked: dynamic calls (target neither Name nor Attribute)
result carries: count, examples, field_used, match_strategy
payload priority: bundle memory_payload > saved artifacts (api 0 > graph 1 > report 2 > other 5 > plan debug 9) > inline planner rows/reply > graph_result/api_result_full/api_result_slim
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re \b39\b
capabilities.example_query: And how many of those were RGATG?
capabilities.gap: RGATG = 39 among the 195 NDMA mice (verified histogram). A number this specific can only come from code that actually ran over the bundle rows in the sandbox; the sandbox's 3-second SIGALRM and AST allow-list are what make failing here mean 'no computation happened', not 'wrong prose'.

capabilities.name: Schema-agnostic JSON profiling for the follow-up prompt
capabilities.description: Summarises an arbitrary result into a bounded skeleton, a list of likely record arrays with their JSON paths, and a field_index classifying each row field as categorical or free_text with distinct-value examples. The field_index is what lets the coder prefer exact equality on a real field over a substring scan — the difference between counting 'male' correctly and matching 'female' too. Parses json_metadata whether it arrives as a dict or a JSON string.
enum_values: output: {root_type, skeleton, record_arrays:[{path, length, examples}], field_index:{row_top_level, row_json_metadata, rows_scanned, note}}
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re \b44\b
capabilities.example_query: How many of those mice have the RG genotype?
capabilities.gap: The single sharpest test of field_index in the whole block. RG is 44 by exact field equality; a substring scan also swallows RGATG (39) and RGA (30) and answers 113. The field_index classifying Genotype as categorical (<=15 distinct values) is precisely what lets the coder prefer equality — this is the 'male vs female' failure in a form we have verified numbers for.

capabilities.name: Fallback: answer the follow-up by feeding the saved result files to the model
capabilities.description: When the code path fails at any stage (payload load, coder call, sandbox execution) this loads every saved artifact of the bundle as text (recursively HTML-stripped; non-JSON files fall back to raw content) and asks the question against that content only. On double failure it returns a degraded message that still reports the prior record count and names both errors.
capabilities.testable_assertion: not expressible — fires only on an internal failure no user query can provoke
capabilities.example_query: How many of those mice have the RG genotype?
capabilities.gap: The legacy path runs only when the fast path fails at payload load, coder call or sandbox execution. No question triggers that; it needs fault injection. And nothing records WHICH path answered: memory_coder_artifact is written on the fast path only (so its absence is suggestive, and 'absent' is not expressible — there is no negated nonempty op), while the double-failure degraded message naming both errors is free prose. Needs a memory_answer_path field ('coder' | 'legacy' | 'degraded'), computable in agents/memory.py:memory_agent_answer where both branches already meet.

capabilities.name: Inject prior bundles and chat history into the prompt
capabilities.description: Two prompt blocks that make follow-ups resolvable at all: a rendering of the last 8 result bundles (id, mode, user_query, endpoint, total) that explicitly says when older bundles exist but are not shown, and a CHAT_HISTORY block of the last N answered turns for pronoun resolution. A per-mode tool summary keeps the logged history token-cheap.
enum_values: recent-results window default: 8 bundles (raised from 3 — long sessions hit a recall cliff)
chat history default: last 5 answered turns
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply mentions NDMA
capabilities.example_query: What was my first search about?
capabilities.gap: Six-turn case: NDMA mice first, four other searches, then this. Tests that the 8-bundle window plus CHAT_HISTORY still reaches turn 1 — the recall cliff that forced the window up from 3 to 8. Answering about the newest search instead is the failure.

capabilities.name: Reuse the last result set by reference ('those samples')
capabilities.description: Walks results_history backwards to the most recent bundle that yields any UIDs (reading rows/nodes/data/samples, stripping HTML, falling back to reporter_plan.uids then parser_plan.filters.uids), and renders a one-line summary of the pinned search. capabilities.name: Top-level parser route enum (7 values) and the single-path parser
capabilities.description: Every NS-engine turn is classified into exactly one of seven execution routes by the parser, which reads the question plus resolved entities, recent bundles, chat history, the REST endpoint catalog and the graph schema, and emits a ParserPlan naming ONE path plus the filters and endpoint that path needs. The field defaults to 'unsupported', so a failure to route is a refusal, not a random search.

capabilities.testable_assertion: parser_plan.mode eq reporter
capabilities.example_query: Put together a summary of the samples IMPACT uploaded last year.
capabilities.gap: Uses a route value no other assertion in this block claims, so the ten cases across the block collectively cover new_search / refine_last_search / ask_about_last_results / system_question / graph_query / reporter — six of the seven. 'unsupported' is deliberately not asserted anywhere: route_policy settled 2026-07-28 that writes and bulk exports are CC's job, and parser_plan.mode resolves to None on any turn that never reaches NS, which is how 3 of the 15 seed-0 failures happened.

capabilities.name: Select (or rank) the target REST endpoint for a search turn
capabilities.description: When the parser picks new_search or refine_last_search it must also name one endpoint from the enriched catalog, choosing the most specific match and treating advanced_search as a last-resort catch-all. It may instead emit ranked endpoint_candidates {endpoint, rationale, confidence}; the field is a permissive union so a model emitting plain strings still validates. An optional semantic shortlist trims the catalog handed to the prompt, off by default and byte-identical when off.
enum_values: POST /nextseek_api/admin/samples/retrieve/ — full metadata + full lineage for explicit UIDs (body field must be 'identifiers'); output_format='excel' gives a workbook
GET /nextseek_api/assays/ — list all assays (titles, types, technologies)
GET /nextseek_api/sample-tree/{uid}/tree/ — bidirectional lineage tree around ONE UID
GET /nextseek_api/sample_types/ — all sample type schema definitions
POST /nextseek_api/sample_types/get_parents/parents_by_child_types/ — parents having derived samples of ALL specified child types
POST /nextseek_api/samples/advanced_search/ — broad attribute/keyword/free-text sample search, paginated
GET /nextseek_api/sops/ — list SOPs/protocols with attachment metadata
rule: advanced_search is the catch-all, used only when no more targeted endpoint fits
semantic shortlist gated by SEMANTIC_ENDPOINTS_ENABLED (default False), dynamic cutoff ratio 0.7 / min_k 10 / max_k 80
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_plan.endpoint eq /nextseek_api/sops/
capabilities.example_query: What SOPs are on file?
capabilities.gap: eq, not contains, so falling through to the advanced_search catch-all fails — that is the rule being tested (most specific match wins; advanced_search is last resort). The endpoint_candidates ranking and the permissive str|EndpointCandidate union are schema concerns with no per-turn outcome, and the semantic endpoint shortlist is byte-identical when off, which it is by default.

capabilities.name: Compose a graph-scope × REST-attribute intersection plan
capabilities.description: When the parser finds both a structural (graph) candidate and an attribute (REST) candidate each covering part of the question, it builds a deterministic 2-step intersect plan: step 1 takes the structural UID scope with all free-text keywords stripped out, step 2 applies the attribute filters, and the executor intersects the UID sets. Skipped when candidate 0 is a high-confidence specialized endpoint, because forcing a graph intersect adds UID-format risk with no benefit.
enum_values: bail-out: candidate 0 is new_search on a non-advanced_search endpoint with confidence >= 0.80
requirement: top structural candidate mode == 'graph_query' and confidence >= 0.60
scope-only rewrite blanks filters['keywords'] and drops metadata['keyword_filter']
capabilities.testable_assertion: parser_plan.mode eq graph_query
capabilities.example_query: Find female mice in the Impact study.
capabilities.gap: Gets the structural half only. The intersect plan is a two-step PlanStep list — step 1 the scope-only graph candidate with filters['keywords'] blanked, step 2 the attribute filters, then a UID-set intersection — and standard-mode debug_payload has no plan key at all, so nothing shows the second step, the intersection, or the bail-out (candidate 0 a non-advanced_search new_search at confidence >= 0.80). The keyword-blanking is not even expressible: there is no negated nonempty op. Needs plan.steps[].tool exposed on query_complete for plan-mode turns.

With no bundle_id every manifest field is None and nothing is written.

capabilities.name: Container-CC artifact publication and download
capabilities.description: After the agent exits, the engine diffs its scratch dir and splits what changed: everything outside scratch/raw/ becomes a downloadable deliverable (zipped when a turn produced more than one), while scratch/raw/ stays on disk as debug output. The terminal reply is deliberately held back until this finishes so it can quote real artifact paths. A separate endpoint serves one artifact by key or a fresh whole-turn zip.

publication shape: {artifacts:[{artifact_type:'file', key:'<turn_id>/<rel>', label, file_format}], raw:[paths], files_created, files_modified}

symlinks and unsafe relpaths refused ('CC: refusing unsafe artifact relpath')
capabilities.testable_assertion: api_artifact.artifacts.zip true — a CC turn that produced more than one deliverable published them as a single zip
capabilities.example_query: Export those NHP samples as a CSV and write me a short README describing the columns.
capabilities.gap: The limit is documented in evaluate.py:113-121 and is real: _publish_artifacts (cc_engine.py:954-961) zips whenever a turn produces >1 deliverable and the MEMBER filenames never reach query_complete, so artifacts.zip is the only addressable name; a single-deliverable turn is addressable only under a filename the agent invented at runtime, which no case can predict. So the criterion proves publication happened but never that the RIGHT files were published, and .rows_gte is always 0 for a CC artifact (indexed under a label with no path). The 'terminal reply held back until publication finishes' contract is likewise unobservable. A cc_artifact_names list field on the payload would fix the first half.

capabilities.name: Sidecar staging sweep and host-path reporting
capabilities.description: Report and submission files staged server-side by the sidecar are swept into the requesting user's own scratch subtree so they surface in the same turn's published artifacts; cross-user delivery is impossible by construction and the destination walk is symlink-safe via an openat chain. Separately, when an op produces a file the agent must quote the HOST-side path, translating container paths with DMAC_PATH_MAPPINGS, and say so explicitly when that variable is missing.
enum_values: sweep modes: same-turn (since_ts set, only this turn's markers) and recovery (since_ts None, all markers)
dir flags O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY; file flags O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW
a _DestUnsafe refuses the WHOLE request dir and preserves the marker
path mapping keys: output, scratch (DMAC_PATH_MAPPINGS, redacted from logs)
the sweep is wrapped in try/except so it must not kill the turn
capabilities.testable_assertion: last_reply matches_re "/dmac/users/[^\s`]+/(output|scratch)/" — the agent quoted the HOST-side logical path of the file it produced, i.e. it read DMAC_PATH_MAPPINGS and translated instead of leaking the container path /data/output
capabilities.example_query: Run a samples report for MetNet and tell me where you put the file.
capabilities.gap: Covers the host-path half only (logical roots come from DMAC_USER_ROOT_MOUNT, default /dmac/users, cc_provision.py:120). The sweep itself is invisible: swept filenames are timestamped (project_<id>_<ts>.uuids.json), a multi-file turn collapses to artifacts.zip, and SweepResult{delivered, deferred_markers} is returned to cc_engine.py:759 and dropped rather than emitted. The cross-user isolation and the O_NOFOLLOW openat chain are properties of the filesystem walk, not of any payload, and belong in cc_staging unit tests. Only delivery-happened could ever be HTTP-visible, and that needs `cc_sweep.delivered`.

capabilities.name: Per-turn REST call ledger
capabilities.description: Each executed REST search appends a record (timestamp, bundle_id, user query, parser plan, api plan, response meta and full data) to the run's api_requests.json so console output stays slim and a wrong answer can be reconstructed later. Listed here as a produced file, not a chat capability.
capabilities.testable_assertion: run_root.api_requests_json.rows_gte gte 1 — the turn appended its executed REST search (bundle_id, parser plan, api plan, response meta and data) to api_requests.json
capabilities.gap: Same root cause as the run-directory capability: api_requests.json lives under the run root, which never appears on query_complete, and it is written by an append-only path (helpers/tools/nextseek_api.py:212 log_api_call) that no-ops when session['api_log_path'] is unset. The atlas itself files this as 'a produced file, not a chat capability' — even with a run_root.* field the natural instrument is a chat_nextseek unit test over log_api_call, not a paid nessie turn.

There is nothing for an HTTP harness to see and NO field should be added — inventing one would manufacture coverage for dead code. The right instrument is a host-lane test asserting the module stays uncalled. Recorded here so nobody writes a case that claims to cover it.

capabilities.name: Scratch-diff artifact detection and post-turn publication

capabilities.gap: The capability's real content is the raw/ SPLIT — everything outside scratch/raw/ becomes a downloadable deliverable, raw/ stays as debug output — and the harness cannot see it, because build_artifact_index MERGES query_complete['artifacts'] and query_complete['cc_raw_files'] into one basename index (evaluate.py:138-141). api_artifact.<name> is therefore true for a raw debug file exactly as for a published deliverable, so no criterion can catch a raw file leaking into the deliverables or a deliverable being misfiled as raw. The payload already carries the two lists separately; the index needs splitting into cc_deliverable.<name> / cc_raw.<name>.

capabilities.gap: Same as the group-82 entry for this endpoint: the driver never issues a GET, so neither the happy path nor the traversal refusal (target.is_relative_to(root)) nor the 'bad key' / 'bad turn_id' 404s are observable. Needs the http_probe.* family plus the turn_id, which the harness does have (the QueryTask id it already polls). Endpoint: nextseek_api/services/cc_assistant.py:783 download_artifact.

capabilities.name: Sidecar staging sweep into the user's scratch
capabilities.description: Report and submission files staged server-side are swept into the requesting user's own scratch subtree so they surface in the same turn's artifacts. Cross-user delivery is impossible by construction and the destination walk is symlink-safe via an openat chain; the sweep is wrapped so it cannot kill the turn.
enum_values: modes: same-turn (since_ts set) and recovery (since_ts None)
_DestUnsafe refuses the WHOLE request dir and preserves the marker

capabilities.gap: A swept file is indistinguishable from an agent-written one once it reaches the merged artifact index, its name is timestamped, and a multi-file turn collapses to artifacts.zip — so there is no criterion that says 'the sweep ran' as opposed to 'the agent wrote something'. The evidence exists but is thrown away: sweep_user_staging returns SweepResult{delivered, deferred_markers} to cc_engine.py:759 and it is never emitted on any event. `cc_sweep.delivered` / `.deferred` would need one line in cc_engine plus a resolver. The safety properties (cross-user impossibility, the O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY chain, _DestUnsafe refusing a whole request dir) are not payload-observable at any price and belong in cc_staging unit tests.

capabilities.name: User file upload into the agent's read-only input dir
capabilities.description: Push files into a persistent per-project input directory the agent sees read-only at /data/input, plus endpoints to poll the job and list what is there. Filenames validated against traversal; the move is cross-device safe.

capabilities.gap: A different endpoint family entirely (POST upload, GET upload/status/<job_id>, GET upload/list) and a different verb: the harness's driver posts one JSON body to query/async/ and has no multipart POST at all (http_driver.py:38-55). So the 202/queued handshake, the PROGRESS/SUCCESS/FAILURE celery states, the 413 over BATCH_UPLOAD_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES and the 400 on duplicate filenames are all unreachable. Needs an `upload_probe.*` family plus a multipart client. Endpoints: nextseek_api/services/cc_assistant.py + cc_upload_tasks.py + cc_upload_validate.py.

Every disk path passes _safe_artifact_path, which resolves symlinks and requires real containment (Path.relative_to, not a string prefix) inside BASE_DIR/outputs or NEXTSEEK_OUTPUTS_DIR.

Both key and turn_id must pass _safe_relpath or the response is 404 'bad key' / 'bad turn_id'. Session ownership is enforced first.

404 no such session | 404 bad key | 404 bad turn_id | 404 not found
