capabilities.description: A scheduled task that summarizes sessions the user never explicitly left, idle past a threshold and whose transcript fingerprint changed. Idempotent.
capabilities.testable_assertion: a session idle past the threshold with a changed transcript is summarized by the sweep
capabilities.gap: Off-turn scheduled work with no chat surface, and the 900s idle threshold puts it outside any run's wall clock. Needs the `cc_summary.*` reader above plus a way to trigger the task; belongs in the container test lane.

capabilities.name: Claude session resume across ephemeral containers
capabilities.description: Claude's own session id is sniffed off the stream, persisted, and passed back as --resume next turn; resume is skipped when the per-session store holds no transcript so it never resumes a session whose transcript is gone.
enum_values: surfaced as cc_session_id, NOT session_id (leaking it as session_id caused the multi-turn 404)
log line: 'cc: resume id present but store empty; starting fresh'
capabilities.testable_assertion: turn 2 of a CC chat recalls a fact that exists only in turn 1's in-container state
capabilities.example_query: turn 1: 'Write the list of NDMA-treated mouse UIDs to a file called cohort_notes.txt in your scratch directory.' turn 2: 'What did you name that file?'

capabilities.name: Durable zstd transcript store with a recovery endpoint
capabilities.description: Each CC turn's complete session .jsonl is compressed into the database so it survives a wiped state dir, and can be downloaded per (session, turn). Decompression is streamed under a hard output cap.
enum_values: cc_session_id required when more than one row matches
capabilities.testable_assertion: GET transcript/{session}/{turn}/ streams the turn's jsonl as application/x-ndjson
capabilities.gap: A different endpoint entirely; the harness only knows query/async/ and tasks/{id}/progress/. Needs a driver that can issue arbitrary GETs plus `transcript.line_count` / `transcript.content_type`.

groups.name: Distilling a finished session into durable memory (Step 1c summarization)

capabilities.name: LLM distillation of one transcript into a SessionSummary
capabilities.description: parse_transcript -> build_actions_view -> BAML b.Summarize (GCPFlash) -> host fills provenance -> apply_grounding. The host OVERWRITES the model's chat_session_id / claude_session_id / transcript_path / transcript_line_count / turn_count / chat_model / writer / summary_model / schema_version / generated_at after the call, so the model cannot forge provenance.
capabilities.testable_assertion: summary.writer == 'baml_gemini' and summary.schema_version == '1c/v1' and summary.transcript_line_count == parse_transcript(raw).line_count, even when the injected summarize_fn returns a SessionSummary with a bogus chat_session_id (host value wins).

capabilities.name: Deterministic actions-only fallback when the summarizer fails
capabilities.description: ANY exception in the summarize path (BAML down, validation error, import failure) is caught and degrades to build_fallback_summary, which walks tool_use blocks and emits one MemoryItem per tool call. A session is never left un-remembered.
capabilities.testable_assertion: with summarize_fn=raise, summary.writer == 'fallback_actions' and summary.summary_model == 'none' and every item.category is MemoryCategory.Artifact and every item.confidence is Confidence.Medium and len(items) <= cfg.max_items (default 8).

capabilities.name: MemoryItem category and confidence closed value sets
capabilities.description: Six categories and three confidence levels, defined in BAML with lowercase aliases and consumed by the renderer's ordering tables.
capabilities.testable_assertion: set(item.category for item in summary.items) is a subset of {preference, context, artifact, decision, todo, fact}, and render_memory emits '## ' sections in exactly the order Decision, Preference, Todo, Artifact, Context, Fact — skipping empty ones.

capabilities.name: Host-side quote grounding — unverified items are flagged, never dropped
capabilities.description: Every EvidenceRef's `verified` bool is recomputed host-side by substring-matching the quote against raw transcript lines [line_start, line_end] (1-based). The model is instructed to always emit verified=false. Items whose quotes do not check out are KEPT and flagged (SPEC-1c §4), so a hallucinated takeaway is visible rather than silently authoritative.
capabilities.testable_assertion: an item whose EvidenceRef.quote does not appear in the cited line range survives into summary.items with evidence[0].verified == False, and its rendered bullet ends with the literal '  _(unverified)_' suffix.

capabilities.name: Numbered actions view + shared tool classifier
capabilities.description: The summarizer is fed a line-numbered 'L<n> <kind>: <detail>' rendering of the transcript, not raw JSON. classify_tool_use is the ONE classifier shared by 1c memory and the Step-3 CCTrace so the two can never drift. Tool outputs are truncated at cfg.truncate_chars with the literal suffix '…[truncated]'.
capabilities.testable_assertion: classify_tool_use({'name':'MultiEdit','input':{'file_path':'/x'}}) == ('edit','MultiEdit','/x'), and build_actions_view over a 3-record transcript emits lines prefixed 'L1 ', 'L2 ', 'L3 ' matching the 1-based raw-line index.

capabilities.name: Change detection: only re-summarize a transcript that actually changed
capabilities.description: fingerprint(raw) = {line_count, sha256 hex}. is_changed compares against extra_state['summary_fingerprint']; no prior fingerprint counts as changed. This is what makes both the per-turn sync summarize and the Celery sweep idempotent.
capabilities.testable_assertion: is_changed(fingerprint(raw), fingerprint(raw)) is False and is_changed(None, fp) is True; a second CC turn with an untouched prior transcript performs zero Summarize calls.

capabilities.name: Where a distilled summary is written (tier + keys)
capabilities.description: The summary is persisted on the SUMMARIZED session's own ChatSession.extra_state under two keys — 'summary' (the SessionSummary dict) and 'summary_fingerprint' — via a single-key read-modify-write that must not clobber siblings. It is NOT written to results_history and NOT to the CCSessionTranscript table.
capabilities.testable_assertion: after a CC turn that syncs session B, ChatSession(B).extra_state has both 'summary' and 'summary_fingerprint' set AND still has its pre-existing 'cc_session_id' key intact.

capabilities.name: Exactly one session is summarized synchronously per CC turn
capabilities.description: select_sync_target picks THE single most-recent CHANGED non-current session, so a turn pays for at most one Summarize call regardless of how many stale sessions the user has. Everything else is left to the Celery sweep.
capabilities.testable_assertion: with three changed non-current sessions, select_sync_target returns only the one with the greatest updated_at, and the turn issues exactly 1 summarize_transcript call; with zero changed sessions it returns None and issues 0.

groups.name: Injecting cross-session memory into a Container-CC turn

capabilities.name: Recency window over the user's OWN other sessions
capabilities.description: select_window takes the `window_size` most-recent sessions by updated_at, excluding the current chat. _session_metas restricts the candidate set to ChatSession.objects.filter(user=user) — never another user's sessions — and skips sessions with no resolvable project dirname. It defers the results_history column because including that multi-MB JSON in the ORDER BY filesort trips MySQL errno 1038.
capabilities.testable_assertion: with 15 prior sessions, len(select_window(metas, current, 10)) == 10, the current session_id is absent, and the list is strictly descending by updated_at; a second user's sessions never appear in metas.

capabilities.name: Deterministic memory markdown (no clock, no randomness)
capabilities.description: render_memory produces the user-tier CLAUDE.md body: a fixed header ('# Cross-session memory (auto-generated — do not edit)'), items grouped by category in _CATEGORY_ORDER and sorted within a category by confidence then session recency, then a '## Recent session transcripts (read-only, on-demand)' block listing one `<mount>/<sid>.jsonl — <gist>` line per window session. Output is a pure function of its inputs.
capabilities.testable_assertion: render_memory(window, fresh_session=False, transcripts_mount=M) called twice on identical inputs returns byte-identical strings, and returns '' when the window is empty OR every window session has zero items.

capabilities.name: fresh_session — clean-room turn with the memory layer disabled
capabilities.description: QueryRequest.fresh_session=true skips the whole 1c layer for this turn: no sync summarize, no window, no rendered memory, no transcripts mount. The 1b in-chat --resume still applies. Any previously written CLAUDE.md is UNLINKED by write_memory_file when the combined markdown is empty, so a stale file cannot leak in.
capabilities.testable_assertion: POST with fresh_session=true performs 0 summarize calls, passes memory_claude_md=None and transcripts_subpath=None to run_cc_turn, and the container's mount list has exactly 3 mounts (input RO, shared RO, scratch RW) plus cc-state — no /home/user/.cc-memory/transcripts mount.

capabilities.name: Atomic memory-file write + byte-copy into the cc-state subpath
capabilities.description: write_memory_file writes tmp+os.replace (atomic on the same fs) and chmods 0644; empty markdown unlinks instead. run_cc_turn then BYTE-COPIES that file into {cc_state_mnt}/CLAUDE.md, because Docker volume subpaths mount directories, not single files. cc-state mounts to /home/user/.claude, so it lands at /home/user/.claude/CLAUDE.md and MERGES with the baked project /home/user/CLAUDE.md.
capabilities.testable_assertion: after a non-fresh CC turn, {user_root_mount}/{project}/{user}/cc-state/{session_id}/CLAUDE.md exists with mode 0644 and content == compose_turn_claude_md(digest, memory); no file named CLAUDE.md.tmp remains.

capabilities.name: Read-only raw-transcript staging for on-demand depth
capabilities.description: stage_transcripts copy-on-change (by size) copies each window session's transcript to {memory_mnt}/transcripts/<sid>.jsonl and PRUNES staged files no longer in the window; returns None when nothing staged so the caller mounts nothing. The dir is mounted read_only at /home/user/.cc-memory/transcripts — deliberately outside .claude so it can never collide with the session store or --resume.
capabilities.testable_assertion: the spawned container's mounts include one with Target == '/home/user/.cc-memory/transcripts', ReadOnly True and VolumeOptions.Subpath == '{project}/{user}/_memory/{session_id}/transcripts'; after a session drops out of the window its <sid>.jsonl is gone from that dir.

capabilities.name: Cross-session memory tuning knobs (env-overridable)
capabilities.description: CCMemoryConfig.from_env. Window size IS the size cap — there is no byte budget. Bad/blank int values fall back to the default rather than raising.
capabilities.testable_assertion: CCMemoryConfig.from_env({'DMAC_CC_MEMORY_WINDOW':'not-an-int'}).window_size == 10 and from_env({'DMAC_CC_MEMORY_WINDOW':'3'}).window_size == 3.

groups.name: Within-chat turn context: the digest a CC turn sees of THIS chat

capabilities.name: NSTurnContext projection — one descriptor per prior NExtSEEK DATA turn
capabilities.description: build_contexts joins chat_log entries that carry an int bundle_id AND an int turn_id to their bundle in results_history. CC entries (mode=='cc'), unrelated turns, error turns and bundle-less entries contribute NOTHING. Malformed bundles are skipped (best-effort). from_bundle derives endpoint/method/total/row_count/truncated/columns/sample_uids and clamps the reply at 2000 chars and sample_uids at 20.
capabilities.testable_assertion: for a chat_log of [NS turn with bundle_id=1, CC turn, NS turn with bundle_id=None], build_contexts returns exactly 1 NSTurnContext with schema_version=='nsctx/v1', bundle_id==1 and full_result_available == (row_count > 0).

capabilities.name: CCTurnContext projection — one descriptor per prior ANSWERED CC turn
capabilities.description: build_cc_contexts keeps only entries with mode=='cc' AND status=='completed' AND an int turn_id. A CC turn has no NS row bundle so the descriptor is just user_query + reply (2000-char cap + reply_truncated flag).
capabilities.testable_assertion: a chat_log CC entry with status=='error' yields zero CCTurnContexts; one with status=='completed' yields exactly one with schema_version=='ccctx/v1' and route=='cc'.

capabilities.name: Rendered within-chat digest with its 10-turn cap and section headers
capabilities.description: render_within_chat_digest emits the NS section first ('## Prior NExtSEEK results in this chat') then the CC section ('## Prior Container-CC turns in this chat'). Each section shows at most DIGEST_MAX_TURNS=10 MOST RECENT turns and, when capped, prepends '(showing the 10 most recent … turns)'. CC replies are whitespace-collapsed and clipped at 200 chars with a '…'. Either section may be empty.
capabilities.testable_assertion: with 12 NS contexts, render_digest output contains the literal '(showing the 10 most recent NS turns)' and exactly 10 lines starting '- turn ', the last of which is turn 12.

capabilities.name: nextseek-recall affordance — CC pulling a prior NS turn's raw rows
capabilities.description: When an NS turn had rows, its digest entry ends with 'recall with `nextseek-recall --turn <N>`'; otherwise '(no raw rows available)'. The op resolves turn_id -> bundle_id via GET session detail?include=turns, downloads the bundle, and materializes rows to /data/scratch/recall/turn-<N>.json. It requires NEXTSEEK_CHAT_SESSION_ID in the agent env (injected per-turn) and has NO latest-bundle fallback.
enum_values: error RECALL_FAILED exit 5 (turn not found / turn has no bundle_id)
capabilities.testable_assertion: nextseek-recall --turn N for an NS turn with rows exits 0 and writes /data/scratch/recall/turn-N.json whose JSON array length == the manifest's row_count; --turn of a CC-only turn exits 5 with code RECALL_FAILED and writes nothing.

capabilities.name: Merge order: within-chat digest FIRST, cross-session memory SECOND
capabilities.description: compose_turn_claude_md joins the two blocks with a blank line, dropping either if empty. This ordering is the contract — this-chat context outranks other-session takeaways in the agent's prompt.
capabilities.testable_assertion: the staged CLAUDE.md contains '## Prior NExtSEEK results in this chat' at a lower index than '# Cross-session memory (auto-generated — do not edit)'; with only memory present the file starts with the memory header and no leading blank lines.

groups.name: Cross-engine memory in both directions (and the CC→NS asymmetry)

capabilities.name: NS → CC: a CC turn sees prior NExtSEEK results (works, high fidelity)
capabilities.description: The NS engine writes both a chat_log entry (chat_memory.append_turn) and a full bundle into results_history. The next CC turn's digest joins them into NSTurnContext with endpoint, total, row_count, columns, up to 20 sample UIDs, filters, and a recall handle. This direction carries STRUCTURE, not just prose.
capabilities.testable_assertion: after turn 1 routes nextseek_query and returns N rows, turn 2's staged CLAUDE.md contains 'turn 1 (bundle 1)' with 'total=<N>' and the sample UIDs from the bundle.

capabilities.name: CC → NS: an NS turn sees prior Container-CC replies (prose only)
capabilities.description: serialize_cc_chat_log_entry writes BOTH assistant_reply (full) and assistant_reply_preview (280-char, debug-block stripped) using the SAME helpers as the NS writer — this was the fix for CC answers being invisible to the next NS turn, because chat_memory.format_for_prompt renders only assistant_reply_preview. The CC entry carries mode='cc', router_choice='container_cc', status='completed', cc_run_id (the run UUID) and cc_traces.
capabilities.testable_assertion: after a completed CC turn, the next NS turn's parser prompt contains a 'CHAT_HISTORY' block with a line '  assistant: <first 280 chars of the CC reply>' — assert serialize_cc_chat_log_entry(...)['assistant_reply_preview'] is non-empty and appears in history_block(session).

capabilities.name: results_history has exactly ONE writer: the NExtSEEK orchestrator
capabilities.description: Result BUNDLES (raw rows, api_plan, files, terminal_reply) are appended only by chat_nextseek.orchestrator via session['results_history'] and persisted by DictSessionAdapter.save(). A Container-CC turn writes NO bundle. Of the CC agent's 13 plugin ops, only `query` (nextseek-query) causes a bundle to exist, and it does so INDIRECTLY by driving the Django assistant endpoint, which runs the NS orchestrator under the same chat session — the other 12 ops go through the sidecar/REST and never touch results_history.
enum_values: op query (writes a bundle, via the assistant endpoint)
capabilities.testable_assertion: len(ChatSession.results_history) is unchanged across a CC turn that runs nextseek-graph / nextseek-api-read / nextseek-report, and increases by exactly 1 across a CC turn that runs nextseek-query.

capabilities.name: The asymmetry's observable: refine_last_search after a CC turn degrades to new_search
capabilities.description: Because a CC turn writes no bundle, an NS follow-up classified refine_last_search finds an empty results_history and would silently build a plan of Nones. _note_refine_without_bundle rewrites mode to 'new_search' and appends a fixed note to plan.notes so the degrade is DETECTABLE. Deliberately not fixed by fabricating a bundle (a synthetic api_plan could be re-POSTed and return confidently wrong rows).
capabilities.testable_assertion: CC turn then 'now narrow that to males' → the reply's debug block / plan.notes contains the literal 'previous turn ran outside the NExtSEEK search path (no result bundle to refine); re-ran as a fresh search' and plan.mode == 'new_search'.

capabilities.name: The shared chat_log entry contract enforced against BOTH writers
capabilities.description: CHAT_LOG_REQUIRED_FIELDS pins the base schema both writers must satisfy: turn_id:int (bool rejected), ts:str, mode:str, user_query:str; assistant_reply is optional but must be a non-empty str when present. next_turn_id derives ids as max(int-coercible turn_ids)+1, skipping str/legacy UUID ids, so it never raises the old `str + int` TypeError and stays correct after FIFO eviction.
capabilities.testable_assertion: validate_chat_log_entry(serialize_cc_chat_log_entry(payload, turn_id=1)) raises nothing, and validate_chat_log_entry({... 'turn_id': True ...}) raises ChatLogEntryError mentioning 'must be int, got bool'; next_turn_id([{'turn_id':'abc'},{'turn_id':7}]) == 8.

capabilities.name: Router history projection from chat_log (the routing layer's memory)
capabilities.description: build_history projects the last MAX_HISTORY_TURNS=5 chat_log entries (ALL kinds — answered, unrelated, error) into typed HistoryTurn, oldest→newest, read BEFORE this turn is appended. Caps are byte-based and UTF-8-boundary-safe. Entries without an int turn_id are skipped; router_choice falls back to a legacy derivation (mode=='cc' → container_cc, else nextseek_query). This is what sticky-CC detection reads.
capabilities.testable_assertion: build_history over 8 entries returns 5 turns ending at the newest; a 600-byte user_query is truncated to <=512 utf-8 bytes plus the '…' character and never splits a codepoint.

groups.name: Durable transcript storage, recovery, and (non-)redaction

capabilities.name: zstd transcript blob per (chat_session, cc_session_id, turn_id)
capabilities.description: After a successful CC turn the raw .jsonl is zstd-compressed (level 10) and written to the CCSessionTranscript table via update_or_create, keyed by (chat_session, cc_session_id, turn_id) where turn_id is the run UUID. It lives in its OWN table, not extra_state, so hot ChatSession reads never load it (SPEC-3 §7/E6). uncompressed_size records the pre-compression byte count. There is no retention/pruning job.
capabilities.testable_assertion: after one CC turn, exactly one CCSessionTranscript row exists with uncompressed_size == len(raw_jsonl) and decompress(row.blob) == raw_jsonl; a Celery retry reusing the same run_id updates that row instead of inserting a second (unique_together).

capabilities.name: Decompression bomb guard on read
capabilities.description: decompress streams in 1MB chunks and raises TranscriptTooLarge once the accumulated output exceeds max_bytes (default 256MB; the endpoint uses settings.CC_TRANSCRIPT_MAX_BYTES with the same default), so a corrupted or hostile row cannot exhaust memory.
capabilities.testable_assertion: decompress(compress(b'x' * 5_000_000), max_bytes=1_000_000) raises TranscriptTooLarge with a message containing 'exceeds 1000000 bytes'.

capabilities.name: Operator transcript recovery endpoint
capabilities.description: GET /nextseek_api/cc-assistant/transcript/{session}/{turn}/ streams the decompressed jsonl as application/x-ndjson with a transcript-{turn}.jsonl attachment name. Ownership is enforced (session filtered by request.user). When several rows share a turn_id and no cc_session_id query param is given it returns 400 'cc_session_id required'; otherwise the newest by created_at wins.
capabilities.testable_assertion: GET the endpoint for another user's session returns 404; with two rows for the same turn and no cc_session_id it returns 400; with the param it returns 200 whose body equals the original jsonl bytes.

capabilities.name: Transcripts are stored UNREDACTED — the only redaction is env-for-logging
capabilities.description: Nothing filters the .jsonl before it is copied to output/raw/, compressed into the DB, staged for cross-session memory, or fed to the summarizer. The single redaction primitive in this subsystem is _redact_env, which masks 9 secret-bearing keys for operational log lines only. A test family must pin this rather than assume redaction exists.
capabilities.testable_assertion: _redact_env({'API_PASS':'s3cret','AWS_REGION':'us-east-1'}) == {'API_PASS':'<REDACTED>','AWS_REGION':'us-east-1'}; and a transcript containing a literal secret string round-trips through compress/decompress byte-identically (no filtering).

capabilities.name: Per-turn raw transcript copy into the user's output tree
capabilities.description: run_cc_turn locates the newest *.jsonl under {cc_state_mnt}/projects with mtime >= turn_start-1, retrying up to 3 times with 0.2s sleeps (the file is written asynchronously by claude), and copies it to {output_mnt}/raw/transcript-{run_id}.jsonl. The basename is guarded by _safe_relpath before the copy.
capabilities.testable_assertion: after a successful CC turn, {output_mnt}/raw/transcript-{run_id}.jsonl exists and its bytes equal the CCSessionTranscript blob's decompressed content; a pre-existing OLDER jsonl (mtime < turn_start-1) is never selected.

capabilities.name: CC_PERSIST_STRICT — fail loudly vs deliver-anyway when persistence breaks
capabilities.description: If the transcript jsonl cannot be found after a successful turn, or on_turn_complete raises, the default behavior is to LOG and still deliver the reply (memory for that turn is lost silently). With settings.CC_PERSIST_STRICT=True (default False) it re-raises, converting the silent memory loss into a query_error.
capabilities.testable_assertion: with no transcript on disk and CC_PERSIST_STRICT=False the turn emits query_complete and logs 'cc persist: missing transcript jsonl'; with True it emits query_error and no chat_log entry is appended for that turn.

groups.name: What a turn's memory activity looks like from outside

capabilities.name: Every CC turn terminates with exactly one query_complete or query_error
capabilities.description: The terminal frame is DEFERRED until after the staging sweep and artifact publish so the reply can report host-side artifact paths (D19). finalize() is a safety net emitting query_complete with reply '(no response)' when the stream ended without a result frame. A non-success result subtype or is_error becomes query_error.
capabilities.testable_assertion: the QueryTask.progress list for any CC turn contains exactly one event in {'query_complete','query_error'}, and it is the LAST entry.

capabilities.name: The four on-disk artifacts that prove memory ran for a turn
capabilities.description: A test can assert memory end-to-end without entering the container: the rendered {memory_mnt}/CLAUDE.md, its copy at {cc_state_mnt}/CLAUDE.md, the staged {memory_mnt}/transcripts/<sid>.jsonl set, and {output_mnt}/raw/transcript-<run_id>.jsonl. All four live under DMAC_USER_ROOT_MOUNT (/dmac/users) inside the nextseek container.
capabilities.testable_assertion: after turn 2 of a chat, all four paths exist and {memory_mnt}/CLAUDE.md is byte-identical to {cc_state_mnt}/CLAUDE.md.

capabilities.name: The recall/query manifest a CC op prints to stdout
capabilities.description: nextseek-recall and nextseek-query emit a single JSON manifest line: {turn_id, bundle_id, total, row_count, columns, path} (query also carries reply, and returns turn_id=None). The `path` is the scratch file the agent then reads, which is how raw NS rows physically cross the engine boundary.
capabilities.testable_assertion: the manifest's row_count equals len(json.load(open(manifest['path']))) and manifest['columns'] equals list(rows[0].keys()) when rows are non-empty.

families.description: Create, name, resume and rehydrate a session; act as the right user or refuse.

groups.name: Keep, name and provision my session

capabilities.name: Persistent session state backends (SQLite or MySQL)
capabilities.description: Session values are JSON-serialized into a session_state(session_id, key, value) table with upsert semantics; placeholder style is translated so the same SQL text works on both backends.
capabilities.testable_assertion: session values round-trip through the session_state table on either backend
capabilities.gap: chat_nextseek-internal storage with no chat surface; the backend is chosen by SESSION_DB_TYPE at config time. Unit-lane against chat_nextseek/session.py.

capabilities.name: Per-project / per-user provisioning with fail-closed project resolution
capabilities.description: Each user's CC tree lives at {project}/{user}/ inside one named volume. The SEEK project is resolved with the user's own credentials; empty membership becomes an isolated personal namespace and any unresolved state rejects the turn rather than guessing.
enum_values: dir kinds: input, shared, scratch, output, cc-state/<session>, _memory/<session>, _memory/<session>/transcripts
shared_subpath deliberately omits the user segment (project-scoped)
refusal: 'Your SEEK project membership changed for this chat. Please start a new chat.'
capabilities.testable_assertion: an unresolvable SEEK project rejects the turn with the fixed refusal instead of guessing a namespace
capabilities.gap: The refusal text ('Could not resolve your SEEK project. Please try again shortly.') arrives as a query_error, so `last_reply` is empty. Needs `last_error`, plus a way to break project resolution. The `last_error` half alone would make this assertable whenever it does occur naturally.

capabilities.name: Automatic chat titling on every route
capabilities.description: Every turn that reaches the end of dispatch titles the chat if it has none, using this turn's query as fallback, so CC and out-of-scope turns no longer leave a chat stuck on 'New chat'.
enum_values: fallback title source: this turn's query (CC / unrelated turns populate no results_history)
capabilities.testable_assertion: a chat whose only turn was container_cc or unrelated still gets a non-default title
capabilities.gap: ChatSession.title is never on the wire -- not on query_complete, not in the POST response. Needs a `session.title` field, reachable through the same ChatSession reader bundle.py already uses. Cheap, and it covers the exact regression this capability exists for (CC/unrelated chats stuck on 'New chat').

groups.name: Act as the right user, or refuse

capabilities.name: Per-turn identity gate with fail-closed impersonation refusal
capabilities.description: Every entry point binds the turn to the asking user's credentials by shallow-copying the config. A request-scoped caller supplying an incomplete pair is REFUSED with a user-facing explanation instead of silently running as the service account; single-operator surfaces (no credentials mapping) warn and proceed.
enum_values: consequence: DRF TOKEN callers are refused
capabilities.testable_assertion: a request-scoped caller supplying half a credential pair is refused rather than run as the service account
capabilities.gap: `debug.identity_refused` WOULD resolve by dot-notation today (it is a plain debug key), so the field exists. What is missing is the stimulus: http_driver always sends a complete Basic header. Needs per-variant credentials in the driver -- and this is a security-relevant capability with zero coverage, so it is worth the plumbing.

capabilities.name: Admin-only controls
capabilities.description: Three privileges are admin-gated and silently downgraded for everyone else: forcing a route, raising the per-turn wall-clock, and the whole evaluator REST surface.
capabilities.testable_assertion: all three admin privileges are silently downgraded for a non-admin
capabilities.gap: Same single-identity blocker as force_route/use_prod/max_turn_length_s, compounded by none of the three privileges being in the driver's request body. Needs per-variant credentials AND the per-turn envelope.

capabilities.name: Credential brokering: the agent holds only the user's NExtSEEK login
capabilities.description: Nine of the thirteen CC ops run server-side in the sidecar; the agent sends {op, args, ns_login, request_id} over a WebSocket and never holds database or provider credentials. An empty api_user is rejected so identities cannot collapse onto one shared staging dir.
enum_values: sidecar ops (9): entity, parse, api-read, api-write, graph, report, generate-submission, run-ls, build-upload-xlsx
viewset ops (4, bypass the sidecar and its write gate): query, plan, pipeline, recall
ws max_size 16 MiB (1 MiB default truncated large responses into a WS 1009 close)
capabilities.testable_assertion: a CC turn's NExtSEEK read succeeds through the sidecar, returning data only the authenticated user can see
capabilities.example_query: Look up how many mouse samples are in the IMPACT study and tell me the number.
capabilities.gap: Proves brokering WORKED. Does not prove the agent holds no other credentials -- that negative needs the env builder inspected (cc_engine._redact_env / _REDACTED_ENV_KEYS), which no wire field reaches. The negative half is the security-relevant half.

groups.name: Session persistence, CC resume, and chat rehydration

capabilities.name: Sniffing and persisting Claude Code's own session id
capabilities.description: make_session_sniffer wraps send_event: the first time an emitted event's data carries a truthy cc_session_id different from the last seen, it invokes on_session_id BEFORE forwarding (last-wins, deduped). The service persists it as extra_state['cc_session_id'] via a single-key merge. It is deliberately surfaced as cc_session_id and NOT session_id — leaking it as session_id caused a multi-turn 404 when the frontend promoted it as the active chat.
capabilities.testable_assertion: after turn 1, ChatSession.extra_state['cc_session_id'] equals the session_id from the container's system/init frame, on_session_id fired exactly once for a stream repeating that id, and no emitted frame contains a top-level 'session_id' equal to the claude uuid.

capabilities.name: --resume is only passed when a transcript actually exists on disk
capabilities.description: store_has_transcripts globs {cc_state_dir}/projects/**/*.jsonl. When a resume id is stored but the store is empty (turn 1, or a wiped volume), effective_session_id is set to None and the turn starts fresh with a log line 'cc: resume id present but store empty; starting fresh' — claude never tries to resume a session whose transcript is gone.
capabilities.testable_assertion: _build_command(model_id=M, session_id=None) contains no '--resume'; with a stored cc_session_id but an empty cc-state dir, the spawned container's command list contains no '--resume'; with a transcript present it ends with ['--resume', <stored id>].

capabilities.name: Per-chat .claude state store mounted across ephemeral containers
capabilities.description: build_user_dirs derives cc_state_subpath = '{project}/{user}/cc-state/{session_id}', mounted RW at /home/user/.claude so transcripts persist across the one-container-per-turn model. Every segment (project dirname, user_id, session_id) is validated against ^[A-Za-z0-9._@+-]{1,128}$ and rejected if '.', '..', contains '/' or NUL, before any interpolation. Backing dirs are mkdir'd + chmod 0777 by Django and a missing subpath is fail-closed BEFORE spawn (the Engine refuses to start otherwise).
capabilities.testable_assertion: build_user_dirs(paths,'2-lab','alice',session_id='..') raises ValueError; a valid call yields cc_state_subpath '2-lab/alice/cc-state/<sid>' and _preflight_subpath_dirs raises FileNotFoundError naming that subpath when the dir is absent.

capabilities.name: Which chat a request lands in (session_id / force_new / most-recent reuse)
capabilities.description: _resolve_session: an explicit session_id is looked up scoped to request.user (a foreign id raises DoesNotExist → 404 'Session not found or you do not own it'); force_new=true always creates; otherwise the most recently updated session of that user is reused, and one is created if none exists. Reusing the most-recent session is what makes an unscoped request inherit a prior chat's memory.
capabilities.testable_assertion: POST with another user's session_id returns 404; POST with force_new=true twice creates two distinct ChatSession rows; POST with an unknown body key returns 422 (extra='forbid').

capabilities.name: Rehydrating a chat in the UI (GET session ?include=turns)
capabilities.description: When chat_log exists it is the source of truth: each entry with a user_query becomes a Turn, reply resolved as assistant_reply > bundle.terminal_reply/reply > assistant_reply_preview, artifacts from the entry or extracted from the bundle, plus cc_traces. True non-answer entries (unrelated / error, no reply and no bundle) are HIDDEN. With no chat_log it falls back to projecting results_history bundles — which is why a CC-only legacy chat rehydrates empty.
capabilities.testable_assertion: GET .../sessions/{id}/?include=turns after [NS turn, CC turn, unrelated turn] returns exactly 2 turns, the CC one with mode=='cc', bundle_id==0 and a non-null cc_traces list, and the unrelated turn absent.

capabilities.name: A chat is pinned to the SEEK project it started in
capabilities.description: The first CC turn stores extra_state['cc_project_dirname']. Every later turn re-resolves the user's project and, if the resolved dirname differs, REFUSES the turn with 'Your SEEK project membership changed for this chat. Please start a new chat.' rather than silently relocating the chat's memory/scratch tree to a different project subpath. Project resolution failure is also fail-closed.
capabilities.testable_assertion: with extra_state['cc_project_dirname']=='2-lab' and resolve_user_project now returning dirname '3-other', the turn emits query_error whose error string contains 'project membership changed' and run_cc_turn is never called.

capabilities.name: Deleting a chat drops its DB memory but not the on-disk store
capabilities.description: DELETE session removes the ChatSession row (cascading CCSessionTranscript rows and with them chat_log / cc_traces / summary / cc_session_id). The volume-backed cc-state transcripts and _memory/<session>/ staging dirs under dmac-cc-users are NOT removed. A deleted session also stops contributing to the cross-session window because _session_metas iterates ChatSession rows.
capabilities.testable_assertion: after DELETE, CCSessionTranscript.objects.filter(chat_session_id=sid).count() == 0 and the session no longer appears in select_window output, while {user_root}/{project}/{user}/cc-state/{sid}/projects/**/*.jsonl still exists on disk.

groups.name: Concurrency and integrity of the memory writes themselves

capabilities.name: refresh-then-merge on every extra_state single-key write
capabilities.description: _merge_extra_state does session.refresh_from_db(fields=['extra_state']) BEFORE merging, because the ChatSession object is loaded at turn start while a nested request on the same session (a different ORM object) can seed keys mid-turn — without the reload, writing cc_session_id would erase a concurrently-seeded pipeline_agent key that the router gate reads next turn. _append_cc_turn_complete does the same.
capabilities.testable_assertion: seed extra_state['pipeline_agent'] from a second ORM instance after the turn's object was loaded, then call _merge_extra_state(session, cc_session_id='x'); reload the row and assert BOTH keys are present.

capabilities.name: DictSessionAdapter.save — row-locked merge for bundles, whole-column overwrite for extra_state
capabilities.description: save() takes select_for_update on the row and merges results_history BY BUNDLE ID (this turn's version wins on conflict) so two concurrent turns cannot erase each other's bundles. extra_state, however, is written as the whole cache minus the typed keys, snapshotted at adapter construction — so it does NOT get the same protection. On a backend without row locking the whole thing falls through to a plain save.
capabilities.testable_assertion: two adapters built from the same stale snapshot, each appending a distinct bundle id, both saved → results_history contains BOTH bundles; but a key written to extra_state between construction and save() of adapter A is absent after A.save().

capabilities.name: FIFO eviction keeps the NEWEST entries
capabilities.description: append_capped returns a NEW list keeping only the last `cap` entries. Newest-kept is load-bearing: a chat_log[:cap] (keep-oldest) mutation must fail the pinned test. Applied identically to chat_log and to the cc_traces mirror, both capped at MAX_CC_CHAT_LOG_TURNS=50.
capabilities.testable_assertion: append_capped(list(range(50)), 'new', cap=50)[-1] == 'new' and [0] == 1 (element 0 evicted), and the input list is unmutated.

capabilities.name: The cc_traces mirror is written in the same shot as chat_log
capabilities.description: apply_turn_to_extra_state appends to BOTH extra_state['chat_log'] and the locked SPEC-3 §6.5 extra_state['cc_traces'] mirror in ONE pure transform, both FIFO-capped so the mirror stays small (it is loaded on every session read). Each trace carries schema_version '3/trace-v1', ordered steps with kind/tool/detail/status/action, a tools_used tally, files_created/modified, and num_turns/duration_ms/cost_usd from the terminal result frame.
enum_values: Step.kind: bash | write | edit | read | skill | tool | text
capabilities.testable_assertion: after one CC turn, len(extra_state['cc_traces']) == 1 and extra_state['chat_log'][-1]['cc_traces'][0]['schema_version'] == '3/trace-v1'; a tool_result with is_error=true sets the matching Step.status == 'error'.

families.description: Timeout, budget cap, max turns, the error taxonomy and failover.

groups.name: Fail safely: error taxonomy, repair and failover

capabilities.name: CC structured error code taxonomy with fixed exit codes
capabilities.description: Every CC op failure emits a one-line JSON error to stderr with a stable code and exit status, and SKILL.md documents the correct agent response for each. The authoritative dict lives in the sidecar contract.
enum_values: RECALL_FAILED (5) — emitted by nextseek-recall but absent from ERROR_EXIT and the SKILL.md table
capabilities.testable_assertion: a failing CC op emits its stable code (e.g. WRITE_BLOCKED) and the documented exit status
capabilities.gap: Codes go to the container's stderr, captured only in the transcript. Needs `cc_trace.steps[].status` (extra_state['cc_traces'], reachable via the ChatSession reader) or a transcript reader. Note RECALL_FAILED is documented as absent from ERROR_EXIT -- a real drift nothing can currently catch.

capabilities.name: LLM failure classification and per-call ledger
capabilities.description: Every structured LLM call is classified into one of five outcomes and written to a ledger with latency, tokens, retry count and stop reason; the classification decides whether the run retries, backs off, fails over or dies.
enum_values: outcome: throttle (429 -> backoff then retry, then LLMFatalError)

ledger fields: agent, provider, model, attempt, outcome, elapsed_ms, timeout_seconds, thinking_budget, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, retry_attempts, bedrock_latency_ms, request_id, stop_reason, error
capabilities.testable_assertion: each structured LLM call lands in exactly one of the five outcomes with its latency and token counts
capabilities.gap: Ledger is a JSONL file under the run's log dir, never on the wire. Would need an `llm_ledger.*` field fed from session['llm_log_path']. Reasonable to add for triage value, but it is instrumentation, not product behaviour.

capabilities.name: Cross-provider failover on 503
capabilities.description: When an agent's provider returns 503 the call is retried against an ordered chain of alternate model profiles, skipping any whose credentials are absent; an exhausted chain raises LLMFatalError('All provider fallbacks exhausted').
capabilities.testable_assertion: a 503 from the primary provider is retried against the next profile in the chain and the turn still answers
capabilities.gap: The harness already detects the EXHAUSTED case (outage.PROVIDER_OUTAGE_MARKER) but a SUCCESSFUL failover is invisible -- the turn just answers. Proving failover ran needs `llm_ledger.provider` or a `failover_count`. Also no way to induce a 503.

capabilities.name: Structured-output repair loop
capabilities.description: Parses model text into the target Pydantic model and on validation failure feeds the errors plus raw output back for a corrected object, up to `retries` times. Provider quirks (code fences, single-element list wrapping) are normalized first.
enum_values: repair prompt: 'Your previous output did not validate for schema {model}. Validation errors: {errors}. Re-output ONLY a corrected JSON object…'
capabilities.testable_assertion: an invalid first model output is repaired within `retries` and the turn still produces a valid plan
capabilities.gap: Only observable as a correct answer, which is indistinguishable from no repair being needed. Needs a `repair_attempts` counter in the ledger. Worth having: the 2026-07-28 review found one line disabling repair for 10 of 17 agents and nothing caught it.

capabilities.name: Fatal LLM error containment
capabilities.description: An LLMFatalError anywhere in a turn is caught, reported as a readable reply, emitted as query_error with fatal=True, and recorded in chat memory as an error turn so the next turn sees no hole in history. LLMFatalError subclasses BaseException deliberately so it bypasses bare `except Exception` in agent code.
enum_values: reply: '**The request could not be completed.**'
run_query re-raises any non-fatal exception after emitting query_error; run_query_plan returns a readable error reply instead
capabilities.testable_assertion: an LLMFatalError yields the fixed readable reply and is recorded as an error turn rather than a hole in history
capabilities.gap: The reply text '**The request could not be completed.**' comes back on query_error, so `last_reply` is empty. Needs `last_error`. Cannot be induced deterministically either, but with `last_error` the assertion would at least be honest whenever it fires.

groups.name: Bound the cost, the blast radius and the network

capabilities.name: Ephemeral sandboxed agent container per turn
capabilities.description: Each CC turn spawns one throwaway `claude` sibling container with private input read-only, project shared dir read-only, per-user read-write scratch and per-session Claude state — always terminating with exactly one query_complete or query_error after publishing.
enum_values: container name: dmac-cc-agent-<run_id> (409 stale-name force-remove retry)
_preflight_subpath_dirs fails closed if a backing dir is missing
capabilities.testable_assertion: a CC turn spawns a container with a working RW scratch mount, evidenced by a file it wrote reaching the caller
capabilities.example_query: Write the UIDs of the NDMA-treated mice into a file called cohort_notes.txt.

capabilities.name: Per-turn cost, turn-count and wall-clock caps

The 2026-07-29 run recorded a task that hit error_max_budget_usd, replied null, and scored GREEN. `last_error` (from the query_error event's data.error, already in the polled payload) fixes this and eight more in group 58.

capabilities.name: De-credentialed agent environment (single-source env builder)
capabilities.description: One function is the sole source of the agent's environment so no secret can sneak in via an inline dict; the agent holds zero AWS credentials, reaching Bedrock only through an auth-proxy sidecar and NExtSEEK only as the authenticated user.

failure: query_error 'Container-CC route is not available: <detail>'

capabilities.gap: query_error again -- needs `last_error`. Provoking it needs the stack broken deliberately. Once `last_error` exists this becomes a useful negative-lane assertion.

descriptor sources: NEXTSEEK_INTERNAL_BASE_URL / NEXTSEEK_BASE_URL / NEXTSEEK_URL, NEO4J_URI, GCP_API_KEY (presence only)

groups.name: Hard limits on a single turn (and the observable when each one trips)

capabilities.name: Per-turn wall-clock timeout (watchdog stop + force-remove)
capabilities.description: A daemon thread waits turn_timeout seconds on a done Event; on expiry it sets a _timed_out flag and calls container.stop(timeout=2) then container.remove(force=True), which ends the stdout stream so the read loop exits. Default 180s. NEXTSEEK_CC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS sets the default but is itself min()'d against NEXTSEEK_CC_TIMEOUT_HARD_MAX (also 180), so raising the ceiling requires setting the HARD_MAX var.
enum_values: NEXTSEEK_CC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default = hard max, clamped to it)
capabilities.testable_assertion: a turn that overruns emits exactly one query_error with reason == 'exec_timeout', agent == 'container_cc' and error == 'Container-CC turn exceeded the 180s limit and was stopped.', NO query_complete follows, and the container name dmac-cc-agent-<run_id> is gone from `docker ps -a`.

capabilities.name: Admin per-request wall-clock override, clamped server-side
capabilities.description: QueryRequest.max_turn_length_s is honored ONLY for is_staff/is_superuser (mirroring the force_route / use_prod gate); non-admins always get the configured default. clamp_turn_timeout maps None/<=0 to the default and otherwise clamps into [30, NEXTSEEK_CC_TIMEOUT_HARD_MAX], so the Debug panel can never exceed what the deployment allows.
capabilities.testable_assertion: clamp_turn_timeout(5) == 30, clamp_turn_timeout(9999) == 180, clamp_turn_timeout(None) == 180, clamp_turn_timeout(90) == 90; a non-admin POST with max_turn_length_s=120 still yields cc_turn_meta.turn_timeout_s == 180.

capabilities.name: Per-turn USD budget cap (claude --max-budget-usd)
capabilities.description: Default $0.50 via NEXTSEEK_CC_MAX_BUDGET_USD; a value of 0 (or falsey) OMITS the flag entirely, disabling the cap. Claude Code stops the turn when accrued cost hits the cap and emits a terminal `result` frame with a non-success subtype, which the translator converts to query_error. The turn's actual spend is surfaced on query_complete as total_cost_usd.
capabilities.testable_assertion: _cc_limit_args(0.50) == ['--max-turns','50','--max-budget-usd','0.5'] and _cc_limit_args(0) == ['--max-turns','50']; a result frame {'subtype':'error_max_budget'} produces ('query_error', {'error':'error_max_budget'...}) and never a query_complete.

capabilities.name: Per-turn agent-loop cap (claude --max-turns)
capabilities.description: Default 50 agent turns inside ONE chat turn, via NEXTSEEK_CC_MAX_TURNS (passed through as a string, always present). Exhaustion surfaces the same way as the budget cap: a non-success terminal result → query_error. The consumed count is reported on query_complete as num_turns and copied into the CCTrace.
capabilities.testable_assertion: the spawned command contains ['--max-turns','50']; a result frame {'subtype':'error_max_turns','is_error':True} yields query_error, and on success extra_state['cc_traces'][-1]['num_turns'] equals the frame's num_turns.

capabilities.name: The nested NExtSEEK turn's own 300s poll deadline inside a 180s CC turn
capabilities.description: When the agent runs nextseek-query, AssistantClient POSTs query/async and polls tasks/{id}/progress with a total deadline of 300s, a 30s per-request timeout and up to 4 retries per poll iteration on transport stalls. Exceeding it yields the sentinel 'stream ended without terminal event'. Because the CC turn's own wall-clock default is 180s, the outer watchdog normally kills the container FIRST — the 300s deadline is only reachable when the hard max has been raised.
capabilities.testable_assertion: with a never-terminal task, run_query returns {'__error__': 'stream ended without terminal event', 'agent': None} after ~300 monotonic seconds and nextseek-query exits 4 (AGENT_FAILED); with default caps the CC turn instead ends in reason=='exec_timeout' at 180s.

capabilities.name: cc_turn_meta — the caps in force are streamed to the Debug panel
capabilities.description: Before spawning, the service emits a cc_turn_meta progress event carrying model_id, the resume cc_session_id (or null), budget_usd and the RESOLVED turn_timeout_s. This is the only place the effective per-turn caps are visible to a user.
capabilities.testable_assertion: the task's progress list contains exactly one {'event':'cc_turn_meta'} whose data.turn_timeout_s == clamp_turn_timeout(requested) and data.budget_usd == 0.5, emitted BEFORE the first agent_started.

capabilities.name: Request-level input cap
capabilities.description: QueryRequest.query is min_length=1, max_length=32000; violation is a 422 validation error before any routing or session work. Batch upload has a separate 200MB total cap (BATCH_UPLOAD_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES) returning 413.
capabilities.testable_assertion: POST with a 32001-char query returns 422 and creates no QueryTask row; POST with '' returns 422.

capabilities.name: A killed turn still lands in memory as a non-answer entry

The finally block then appends a chat_log entry with status='error', the error text, mode derived from router_choice, and NO assistant_reply — via the adapter when NS ran, or via a refresh-then-RMW on extra_state otherwise. This is why a timed-out CC turn does not make the chat sticky and does not appear in the rehydrated UI.
capabilities.testable_assertion: after an exec_timeout CC turn, chat_log[-1] == {'turn_id':N,'ts':...,'mode':'cc','user_query':Q,'router_choice':'container_cc','status':'error','error':'Container-CC turn exceeded the 180s limit and was stopped.'} with no assistant_reply key, and the NEXT turn is not sticky-converted to CC.

capabilities.name: Silent truncation caps applied to remembered text

memory items 8 per session; window 10 sessions
memory_coder profile 50000 chars; computed result 60000 chars

capabilities.testable_assertion: the Streamlit stepper maps each event agent to its human label

groups.name: Turn delivery: submit, stream, poll

capabilities.name: POST /nextseek_api/cc-assistant/query/async/ (the routed chat entry point)
capabilities.description: The endpoint the chat UI actually posts to. Validates QueryRequest, resolves the session, creates a QueryTask(status='running'), spawns a daemon thread, and returns HTTP 202 {task_id, session_id} immediately. Routing (RG-1..RG-4) happens inside the worker, so a routing outcome is only observable via the progress stream, never in the HTTP response.
capabilities.testable_assertion: POST returns 202 with a task_id and session_id, and the response body contains no `route` field (the route is only in the progress stream's first event).

capabilities.name: POST /nextseek_api/cc-assistant/cc/query/async/ (force Container-CC)
capabilities.description: Identical envelope and response to RG-8.1 but calls _start_task(force_cc=True), skipping the router. Not exercised by the frontend; used by harnesses and operators.
capabilities.testable_assertion: POST to this path with "how many mice do we have" produces route_decided.source=="forced" and route=="container_cc".

capabilities.name: POST /nextseek_api/assistant/query/ (SSE streaming, NS-only)
capabilities.description:
The pre-router streaming entry point. Runs chat_nextseek in a thread feeding a queue.Queue, and streams 'event: <type>
data: <json>

' frames with Cache-Control no-cache and X-Accel-Buffering no. No router is consulted — this endpoint always runs the NExtSEEK engine, and it honors only mode 'plan' vs default. A None sentinel closes the stream.
capabilities.testable_assertion: POST with a CC-flavoured query ("write me a python script") still runs chat_nextseek.orchestrator.run_query and the SSE stream contains no route_decided event.

capabilities.name: POST /nextseek_api/assistant/query/async/ (async, NS-only, has the pipeline mode)
capabilities.description: Same async shape as RG-8.1 but no router: always the NExtSEEK engine, with the three-way mode dispatch (plan / pipeline / standard). This is the only endpoint that reaches run_pipeline_launch.
capabilities.testable_assertion: POST mode="pipeline" here calls run_pipeline_launch exactly once and emits no route_decided event.

capabilities.name: GET tasks/{task_id}/progress/ (poll fallback, both viewsets)
capabilities.description: The same response shape is served at TWO paths: /nextseek_api/assistant/tasks/{task_id}/progress/ and /nextseek_api/cc-assistant/tasks/{task_id}/progress/. Both filter by task_id AND request.user (404 otherwise) and both suppress `result` until the task is terminal. The frontend uses this only when the websocket fails to open.
enum_values: response fields: task_id, session_id, status, progress[], result?
result present only when status in (completed, error)
404: "Task not found or you do not own it."
capabilities.testable_assertion: While status=="running" the response's result is null even though QueryTask.result may already hold data; another user's task_id returns 404 on both paths.

capabilities.name: WS ws/assistant/progress/{task_id}/ (primary transport)
capabilities.description: The single existing consumer both engines stream through, so chat_frontend needs no per-route code. Polls QueryTask every 300 ms, pushes new events, sends a final `done` frame at a terminal status and closes. Requires an authenticated user AND ownership — the task UUID is explicitly not a capability token. Browser WS cannot send Authorization headers, so Basic/Token-only clients are anonymous here and must fall back to RG-8.5. Origin is checked against CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS + CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS (a missing Origin header is allowed).
capabilities.testable_assertion: Connecting with a valid task_id but no authenticated session is rejected; connecting as the owner yields the route_decided event followed eventually by a done frame and a close.

capabilities.name: QueryTask status machine and event persistence
capabilities.description: make_db_event_callback appends every {event, data} to QueryTask.progress and flips status on terminal events: query_complete -> completed (result = payload), query_error -> error (result = payload). It also stamps session_id onto both terminal payloads via setdefault. The routed endpoint wraps this callback with wrap_send_event so the first query_error is recorded for the non-answer writeback (RG-5.6).
capabilities.testable_assertion: After a turn emitting agent_started, query_complete: QueryTask.status == "completed", result == the query_complete payload, and result["session_id"] equals the resolved session id even though the emitter omitted it.

capabilities.name: Worker-level failure envelopes on the routed endpoint
capabilities.description: Three distinct failure paths all surface as a query_error event (never an HTTP error, since the HTTP 202 already returned): an unhandled worker exception -> {error: 'Internal pipeline error', agent: 'unknown'}; cc_runner_available() false -> {error: 'Container-CC route is not available: <detail>', agent: 'container_cc'}; SEEK project resolution failure or a changed project membership mid-chat -> a user-facing message with agent 'container_cc'.
enum_values: error: Container-CC route is not available: docker daemon unreachable: <ExcType>
error: Container-CC route is not available: CC image '' not found
error: Container-CC route is not available: CC network '<net>' not found
error: Could not resolve your SEEK project. Please try again shortly.
error: Your SEEK project membership changed for this chat. Please start a new chat.
capabilities.testable_assertion: With the docker daemon unreachable, a container_cc-routed turn yields QueryTask.status=="error" and result["error"].startswith("Container-CC route is not available: docker daemon unreachable") after the route_decided event was already emitted.

capabilities.name: Session resolution and credential resolution at turn start
capabilities.description: Before routing, _start_task resolves the session (RG-6.4/6.5), creates the QueryTask, and resolves credentials via resolve_seek_auth(['BASIC','SESSION']) falling back to request.session['username']/['password']. It keeps TWO credential pairs: the possibly prod-swapped (api_user, api_pass) for the NS engine, and the untouched (user_api_user, user_api_pass) for CC's project resolution and container env.
enum_values: credential sources in order: Basic header, Django session username/password
prod swap applies only to the NS-route pair
capabilities.testable_assertion: With use_prod=true as admin on a CC-routed turn, cc_provision.resolve_user_project is called with the requesting user's credentials, not NEXTSEEK_CHAT_CONFIG_PROD.API_USER.

groups.name: Behave safely inside the sandbox (CC agent contract)

capabilities.name: Write safety — the three-layer contract
capabilities.description: Every non-GET NExtSEEK operation passes a Claude Code permission allowlist (defense in depth), a mechanical server-side confirmation gate the agent cannot bypass, and a behavioural plain-text confirmation obtained from the user first.
enum_values: L1 allowlist (setup.sh): nextseek-entity-extract, nextseek-parse, nextseek-plan, nextseek-api-read --parser-plan*, nextseek-graph, nextseek-report --mode samples/protocols/published/rppr, nextseek-generate-submission --type, nextseek-pipeline, nextseek-run-ls, nextseek-build-upload-xlsx, nextseek-project-resolve, nextseek-sampletype-attrs, nextseek-sample-search, nextseek-assay-resolve, nextseek-build-payload, nextseek-validate-upload, nextseek-extract-text — nextseek-api-write is deliberately ABSENT
L2: sidecar write_gate.py refuses unless confirmed_write is exactly True (WRITE_BLOCKED exit 5)
L3: plain-text confirmation prompt before invoking the write
capabilities.testable_assertion: a write request is not executed until the agent has obtained a plain-text confirmation

criterion.value: (?i)(confirm|shall I|should I|do you want me to|are you sure)

capabilities.example_query: Register a new mouse sample for the NDMA study.
capabilities.gap: Only layer L3 (the behavioural prompt) is visible. L1 (the Claude Code allowlist, with nextseek-api-write deliberately absent) and L2 (the sidecar write_gate refusing unless confirmed_write is exactly True, WRITE_BLOCKED exit 5) leave no trace on the wire. `cc_trace.tools_used` would expose L1; the sidecar's WRITE_BLOCKED needs a sidecar-side observable.

capabilities.name: Stop-after-2 rule and the hard prohibitions
capabilities.description: A hard two-attempt budget per user question across ALL nextseek-* tools combined. After a second failure the agent must stop and reply in plain text with what it tried, the error and one clarifying question — and is forbidden from spelunking plugin source to reverse-engineer the failure.
enum_values: prohibited after a failure: Read any file under /app/plugins/nextseek/bin/
prohibited: sibling-op preflight to reverse-engineer the failure
capabilities.testable_assertion: after two failed nextseek-* attempts the agent stops and replies in plain text instead of spelunking plugin source
capabilities.gap: Needs `cc_trace.steps` to count attempts and to show that no Read/Grep over /app/plugins/nextseek/bin/ followed.
